/home/redkidd/SoloTime/HedgeyFund/valari/valari-contracts/lib/forge-std/src/StdChains.sol
   1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0
   2 |     | pragma solidity >=0.8.13 <0.9.0;
   3 |     | 
   4 |     | import {VmSafe} from "./Vm.sol";
   5 |     | 
   6 |     | /**
   7 |     |  * StdChains provides information about EVM compatible chains that can be used in scripts/tests.
   8 |     |  * For each chain, the chain's name, chain ID, and a default RPC URL are provided. Chains are
   9 |     |  * identified by their alias, which is the same as the alias in the `[rpc_endpoints]` section of
  10 |     |  * the `foundry.toml` file. For best UX, ensure the alias in the `foundry.toml` file matches the
  11 |     |  * alias used in this contract, which can be found as the first argument to the
  12 |     |  * `_setChainWithDefaultRpcUrl` call in the `_initializeStdChains` function.
  13 |     |  *
  14 |     |  * There are two main ways to use this contract:
  15 |     |  *   1. Set a chain with `setChain(string memory chainAlias, ChainData memory chain)` or
  16 |     |  *      `setChain(string memory chainAlias, Chain memory chain)`
  17 |     |  *   2. Get a chain with `getChain(string memory chainAlias)` or `getChain(uint256 chainId)`.
  18 |     |  *
  19 |     |  * The first time either of those are used, chains are initialized with the default set of RPC URLs.
  20 |     |  * This is done in `_initializeStdChains`, which uses `_setChainWithDefaultRpcUrl`. Defaults are recorded in
  21 |     |  * `_defaultRpcUrls`.
  22 |     |  *
  23 |     |  * The `setChain` function is straightforward, and it simply saves off the given chain data.
  24 |     |  *
  25 |     |  * The `getChain` methods use `_getChainWithUpdatedRpcUrl` to return a chain. For example, let's say
  26 |     |  * we want to retrieve the RPC URL for `mainnet`:
  27 |     |  *   - If you have specified data with `setChain`, it will return that.
  28 |     |  *   - If you have configured a mainnet RPC URL in `foundry.toml`, it will return the URL, provided it
  29 |     |  *     is valid (e.g. a URL is specified, or an environment variable is given and exists).
  30 |     |  *   - If neither of the above conditions is met, the default data is returned.
  31 |     |  *
  32 |     |  * Summarizing the above, the prioritization hierarchy is `setChain` -> `foundry.toml` -> environment variable -> defaults.
  33 |     |  */
  34 |     | abstract contract StdChains {
  35 |     |     VmSafe private constant vm = VmSafe(address(uint160(uint256(keccak256("hevm cheat code")))));

  45 |     |     struct Chain {
  46 |     |         // The chain name.
  47 |     |         string name;
  48 |     |         // The chain's Chain ID.
  49 |     |         uint256 chainId;
  50 |     |         // The chain's alias. (i.e. what gets specified in `foundry.toml`).
  51 |     |         string chainAlias;
  52 |     |         // A default RPC endpoint for this chain.
  53 |     |         // NOTE: This default RPC URL is included for convenience to facilitate quick tests and
  54 |     |         // experimentation. Do not use this RPC URL for production test suites, CI, or other heavy
  55 |     |         // usage as you will be throttled and this is a disservice to others who need this endpoint.
  56 |     |         string rpcUrl;
  57 |     |     }
  58 |     | 
  59 |     |     // Maps from the chain's alias (matching the alias in the `foundry.toml` file) to chain data.

  61 |     |     // Maps from the chain's alias to its default RPC URL.
  62 |     |     mapping(string => string) private _defaultRpcUrls;
  63 |     |     // Maps from a chain ID to its alias.

  68 |     |     /// @notice Returns chain data for the given alias, with the RPC URL resolved from config or defaults.
  69 |     |     /// @dev Reverts if `chainAlias` is empty or has not been registered.
  70 |     |     function getChain(string memory chainAlias) internal virtual returns (Chain memory chain) {
  71 |     |         require(bytes(chainAlias).length != 0, "StdChains getChain(string): Chain alias cannot be the empty string.");
  72 |     | 
  73 |     |         _initializeStdChains();
  74 |     |         chain = _chains[chainAlias];
  75 |     |         require(
  76 |     |             chain.chainId != 0,
  77 |     |             string(abi.encodePacked("StdChains getChain(string): Chain with alias \"", chainAlias, "\" not found."))
  78 |     |         );
  79 |     | 
  80 |     |         chain = _getChainWithUpdatedRpcUrl(chainAlias, chain);
  81 |     |     }

  83 |     |     /// @notice Returns chain data for the given chain ID, with the RPC URL resolved from config or defaults.
  84 |     |     /// @dev Reverts if `chainId` is `0` or has not been registered.
  85 |     |     function getChain(uint256 chainId) internal virtual returns (Chain memory chain) {
  86 |     |         require(chainId != 0, "StdChains getChain(uint256): Chain ID cannot be 0.");

  88 |     |         string memory chainAlias = _idToAlias[chainId];

  95 |     |         );
  96 |     | 
  97 |     |         chain = _getChainWithUpdatedRpcUrl(chainAlias, chain);

 100 |     |     /// @notice Registers chain data under `chainAlias`, with priority given to the argument's `rpcUrl` field.
 101 |     |     function setChain(string memory chainAlias, ChainData memory chain) internal virtual {
 102 |     |         require(
 103 |     |             bytes(chainAlias).length != 0,
 104 |     |             "StdChains setChain(string,ChainData): Chain alias cannot be the empty string."
 105 |     |         );
 106 |     | 
 107 |     |         require(chain.chainId != 0, "StdChains setChain(string,ChainData): Chain ID cannot be 0.");
 108 |     | 
 109 |     |         _initializeStdChains();
 110 |     |         string memory foundAlias = _idToAlias[chain.chainId];
 111 |     | 
 112 |     |         require(
 113 |     |             bytes(foundAlias).length == 0 || keccak256(bytes(foundAlias)) == keccak256(bytes(chainAlias)),
 114 |     |             string(
 115 |     |                 abi.encodePacked(
 116 |     |                     "StdChains setChain(string,ChainData): Chain ID ",
 117 |     |                     vm.toString(chain.chainId),
 118 |     |                     " already used by \"",
 119 |     |                     foundAlias,
 120 |     |                     "\"."
 121 |     |                 )
 122 |     |             )
 123 |     |         );
 124 |     | 
 125 |     |         uint256 oldChainId = _chains[chainAlias].chainId;
 126 |     |         delete _idToAlias[oldChainId];
 127 |     | 
 128 |     |         _chains[chainAlias] =
 129 |     |             Chain({name: chain.name, chainId: chain.chainId, chainAlias: chainAlias, rpcUrl: chain.rpcUrl});
 130 |     |         _idToAlias[chain.chainId] = chainAlias;
 131 |     |     }
 132 |     | 
 133 |     |     /// @notice Registers chain data under `chainAlias`, with priority given to the argument's `rpcUrl` field.
 134 |     |     function setChain(string memory chainAlias, Chain memory chain) internal virtual {
 135 |     |         setChain(chainAlias, ChainData({name: chain.name, chainId: chain.chainId, rpcUrl: chain.rpcUrl}));
 136 |     |     }

 138 |     |     function _toUpper(string memory str) private pure returns (string memory) {
 139 |     |         bytes memory strb = bytes(str);
 140 |     |         bytes memory copy = new bytes(strb.length);
 141 |     |         for (uint256 i = 0; i < strb.length; i++) {
 142 |     |             bytes1 b = strb[i];
 143 |     |             if (b >= 0x61 && b <= 0x7A) {
 144 |     |                 copy[i] = bytes1(uint8(b) - 32);
 145 |     |             } else {
 146 |     |                 copy[i] = b;
 147 |     |             }
 148 |     |         }
 149 |     |         return string(copy);
 150 |     |     }
 151 |     | 
 152 |     |     // lookup rpcUrl, in descending order of priority:
 153 |     |     // current -> config (foundry.toml) -> environment variable -> default
 154 |     |     function _getChainWithUpdatedRpcUrl(string memory chainAlias, Chain memory chain)
 155 |     |         private
 156 |     |         view
 157 |     |         returns (Chain memory)
 158 |     |     {
 159 |     |         if (bytes(chain.rpcUrl).length == 0) {
 160 |     |             try vm.rpcUrl(chainAlias) returns (string memory configRpcUrl) {
 161 |     |                 chain.rpcUrl = configRpcUrl;
 162 |     |             } catch (bytes memory err) {
 163 |     |                 string memory envName = string(abi.encodePacked(_toUpper(chainAlias), "_RPC_URL"));
 164 |     |                 if (_fallbackToDefaultRpcUrls) {
 165 |     |                     chain.rpcUrl = vm.envOr(envName, _defaultRpcUrls[chainAlias]);
 166 |     |                 } else {
 167 |     |                     chain.rpcUrl = vm.envString(envName);
 168 |     |                 }
 169 |     |                 // Distinguish 'not found' from 'cannot read'
 170 |     |                 // The upstream error thrown by forge for failing cheats changed so we check both the old and new versions
 171 |     |                 bytes memory oldNotFoundError =
 172 |     |                     abi.encodeWithSignature("CheatCodeError", string(abi.encodePacked("invalid rpc url ", chainAlias)));
 173 |     |                 bytes memory newNotFoundError = abi.encodeWithSignature(
 174 |     |                     "CheatcodeError(string)", string(abi.encodePacked("invalid rpc url: ", chainAlias))
 175 |     |                 );
 176 |     |                 bytes32 errHash = keccak256(err);
 177 |     |                 if (
 178 |     |                     (errHash != keccak256(oldNotFoundError) && errHash != keccak256(newNotFoundError))
 179 |     |                         || bytes(chain.rpcUrl).length == 0
 180 |     |                 ) {
 181 |     |                     assembly ("memory-safe") {
 182 |     |                         revert(add(32, err), mload(err))
 183 |     |                     }
 184 |     |                 }
 185 |     |             }
 186 |     |         }
 187 |     |         return chain;
 188 |     |     }

 191 |     |     }
 192 |     | 
 193 |     |     struct Account {
 194 |     |         address addr;
 195 |     |         uint256 key;
 196 |     |     }
 197 |     | 
 198 |     |     enum AddressType {
 199 |     |         Payable,
 200 |     |         NonPayable,
 201 |     |         ZeroAddress,
 202 |     |         Precompile,
 203 |     |         ForgeAddress
 204 |     |     }

 206 |     |     /// @notice Assumes `addr` is not blacklisted by `token`, skipping the fuzz run if it is.
 207 |     |     function assumeNotBlacklisted(address token, address addr) internal view virtual {
 208 |     |         // Nothing to check if `token` is not a contract.
 209 |     |         uint256 tokenCodeSize;
 210 |     |         assembly {
 211 |     |             tokenCodeSize := extcodesize(token)
 212 |     |         }
 213 |     |         require(tokenCodeSize > 0, "StdCheats assumeNotBlacklisted(address,address): Token address is not a contract.");
 214 |     | 
 215 |     |         bool success;
 216 |     |         bytes memory returnData;
 217 |     | 
 218 |     |         // 4-byte selector for `isBlacklisted(address)`, used by USDC.
 219 |     |         (success, returnData) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(0xfe575a87, addr));
 220 |     |         vm.assume(!success || abi.decode(returnData, (bool)) == false);
 221 |     | 
 222 |     |         // 4-byte selector for `isBlackListed(address)`, used by USDT.
 223 |     |         (success, returnData) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(0xe47d6060, addr));
 224 |     |         vm.assume(!success || abi.decode(returnData, (bool)) == false);
 225 |     |     }
 226 |     | 
 227 |     |     /// @notice Assumes `addr` is not blacklisted by `token`, skipping the fuzz run if it is.
 228 |     |     /// @dev Deprecated alias for `assumeNotBlacklisted`. Will be removed in a future breaking release.
 229 |     |     function assumeNoBlacklisted(address token, address addr) internal view virtual {
 230 |     |         assumeNotBlacklisted(token, addr);
 231 |     |     }
 232 |     | 
 233 |     |     /// @notice Assumes `addr` does not match `addressType`, skipping the fuzz run if it does.
 234 |     |     function assumeAddressIsNot(address addr, AddressType addressType) internal virtual {
 235 |     |         if (addressType == AddressType.Payable) {
 236 |     |             assumeNotPayable(addr);
 237 |     |         } else if (addressType == AddressType.NonPayable) {
 238 |     |             assumePayable(addr);
 239 |     |         } else if (addressType == AddressType.ZeroAddress) {
 240 |     |             assumeNotZeroAddress(addr);
 241 |     |         } else if (addressType == AddressType.Precompile) {
 242 |     |             assumeNotPrecompile(addr);
 243 |     |         } else if (addressType == AddressType.ForgeAddress) {
 244 |     |             assumeNotForgeAddress(addr);
 245 |     |         }
 246 |     |     }
 247 |     | 
 248 |     |     /// @notice Assumes `addr` does not match `addressType1` or `addressType2`, skipping the fuzz run if it does.
 249 |     |     function assumeAddressIsNot(address addr, AddressType addressType1, AddressType addressType2) internal virtual {
 250 |     |         assumeAddressIsNot(addr, addressType1);
 251 |     |         assumeAddressIsNot(addr, addressType2);
 252 |     |     }
 253 |     | 
 254 |     |     /// @notice Assumes `addr` does not match any of the three given address types, skipping the fuzz run if it does.
 255 |     |     function assumeAddressIsNot(
 256 |     |         address addr,
 257 |     |         AddressType addressType1,
 258 |     |         AddressType addressType2,
 259 |     |         AddressType addressType3
 260 |     |     ) internal virtual {
 261 |     |         assumeAddressIsNot(addr, addressType1);
 262 |     |         assumeAddressIsNot(addr, addressType2);
 263 |     |         assumeAddressIsNot(addr, addressType3);
 264 |     |     }
 265 |     | 
 266 |     |     /// @notice Assumes `addr` does not match any of the four given address types, skipping the fuzz run if it does.
 267 |     |     function assumeAddressIsNot(
 268 |     |         address addr,
 269 |     |         AddressType addressType1,
 270 |     |         AddressType addressType2,
 271 |     |         AddressType addressType3,
 272 |     |         AddressType addressType4
 273 |     |     ) internal virtual {
 274 |     |         assumeAddressIsNot(addr, addressType1);
 275 |     |         assumeAddressIsNot(addr, addressType2);
 276 |     |         assumeAddressIsNot(addr, addressType3);
 277 |     |         assumeAddressIsNot(addr, addressType4);
 278 |     |     }
 279 |     | 
 280 |     |     // This function checks whether an address, `addr`, is payable. It works by sending 1 wei to
 281 |     |     // `addr` and checking the `success` return value.
 282 |     |     // NOTE: This function may result in state changes depending on the fallback/receive logic
 283 |     |     // implemented by `addr`, which should be taken into account when this function is used.
 284 |     |     function _isPayable(address addr) private returns (bool) {
 285 |     |         require(
 286 |     |             addr.balance < _UINT256_MAX,
 287 |     |             "StdCheats _isPayable(address): Balance equals max uint256, so it cannot receive any more funds"
 288 |     |         );
 289 |     |         uint256 origBalanceTest = address(this).balance;
 290 |     |         uint256 origBalanceAddr = address(addr).balance;
 291 |     | 
 292 |     |         vm.deal(address(this), 1);
 293 |     |         (bool success,) = payable(addr).call{value: 1}("");
 294 |     | 
 295 |     |         // reset balances
 296 |     |         vm.deal(address(this), origBalanceTest);
 297 |     |         vm.deal(addr, origBalanceAddr);
 298 |     | 
 299 |     |         return success;
 300 |     |     }
 301 |     | 
 302 |     |     /// @notice Assumes `addr` is a payable address, skipping the fuzz run if it is not.
 303 |     |     /// @dev May cause state changes depending on `addr`'s fallback or receive logic.
 304 |     |     function assumePayable(address addr) internal virtual {
 305 |     |         vm.assume(_isPayable(addr));
 306 |     |     }
 307 |     | 
 308 |     |     /// @notice Assumes `addr` is not a payable address, skipping the fuzz run if it is.
 309 |     |     /// @dev May cause state changes depending on `addr`'s fallback or receive logic.
 310 |     |     function assumeNotPayable(address addr) internal virtual {
 311 |     |         vm.assume(!_isPayable(addr));
 312 |     |     }
 313 |     | 
 314 |     |     /// @notice Assumes `addr` is not the zero address, skipping the fuzz run if it is.
 315 |     |     function assumeNotZeroAddress(address addr) internal pure virtual {
 316 |     |         vm.assume(addr != address(0));
 317 |     |     }
 318 |     | 
 319 |     |     /// @notice Assumes `addr` is not a precompile on the current chain, skipping the fuzz run if it is.
 320 |     |     function assumeNotPrecompile(address addr) internal pure virtual {
 321 |     |         assumeNotPrecompile(addr, _pureChainId());
 322 |     |     }
 323 |     | 
 324 |     |     /// @notice Assumes `addr` is not a precompile on `chainId`, skipping the fuzz run if it is.
 325 |     |     function assumeNotPrecompile(address addr, uint256 chainId) internal pure virtual {
 326 |     |         // Note: For some chains like Optimism these are technically predeploys (i.e. bytecode placed at a specific
 327 |     |         // address), but the same rationale for excluding them applies so we include those too.
 328 |     | 
 329 |     |         // These are reserved by Ethereum and may be on all EVM-compatible chains.
 330 |     |         vm.assume(addr < address(0x1) || addr > address(0xff));
 331 |     | 
 332 |     |         // forgefmt: disable-start
 333 |     |         if (chainId == 10 || chainId == 420 || chainId == 11155420) {
 334 |     |             // https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/eaa371a0184b56b7ca6d9eb9cb0a2b78b2ccd864/op-bindings/predeploys/addresses.go#L6-L21
 335 |     |             vm.assume(addr < address(0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000000) || addr > address(0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000800));
 336 |     |         } else if (chainId == 42161 || chainId == 421613) {
 337 |     |             // https://developer.arbitrum.io/useful-addresses#arbitrum-precompiles-l2-same-on-all-arb-chains
 338 |     |             vm.assume(addr < address(0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000064) || addr > address(0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000068));
 339 |     |         } else if (chainId == 43114 || chainId == 43113) {
 340 |     |             // https://github.com/ava-labs/subnet-evm/blob/47c03fd007ecaa6de2c52ea081596e0a88401f58/precompile/params.go#L18-L59
 341 |     |             vm.assume(addr < address(0x0100000000000000000000000000000000000000) || addr > address(0x01000000000000000000000000000000000000ff));
 342 |     |             vm.assume(addr < address(0x0200000000000000000000000000000000000000) || addr > address(0x02000000000000000000000000000000000000FF));
 343 |     |             vm.assume(addr < address(0x0300000000000000000000000000000000000000) || addr > address(0x03000000000000000000000000000000000000Ff));
 344 |     |         }
 345 |     |         // forgefmt: disable-end
 346 |     |     }
 347 |     | 
 348 |     |     /// @notice Assumes `addr` is not a Forge-reserved address (vm, console, Create2Deployer), skipping the fuzz run if it is.
 349 |     |     function assumeNotForgeAddress(address addr) internal pure virtual {
 350 |     |         // vm, console, and Create2Deployer addresses
 351 |     |         vm.assume(
 352 |     |             addr != address(vm) && addr != 0x000000000000000000636F6e736F6c652e6c6f67
 353 |     |                 && addr != 0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C
 354 |     |         );
 355 |     |     }
 356 |     | 
 357 |     |     /// @notice Assumes `addr` has no code and is not a precompile, zero, or Forge-reserved address.
 358 |     |     function assumeUnusedAddress(address addr) internal view virtual {
 359 |     |         uint256 size;
 360 |     |         assembly {
 361 |     |             size := extcodesize(addr)
 362 |     |         }
 363 |     |         vm.assume(size == 0);
 364 |     | 
 365 |     |         assumeNotPrecompile(addr);
 366 |     |         assumeNotZeroAddress(addr);
 367 |     |         assumeNotForgeAddress(addr);
 368 |     |     }

 370 |     |     /// @notice Reads and parses an EIP-1559 broadcast artifact from `path`.
 371 |     |     function readEIP1559ScriptArtifact(string memory path)
 372 |     |         internal
 373 |     |         view
 374 |     |         virtual
 375 |     |         returns (EIP1559ScriptArtifact memory)
 376 |     |     {
 377 |     |         string memory data = vm.readFile(path);
 378 |     |         bytes memory parsedData = vm.parseJson(data);
 379 |     |         RawEIP1559ScriptArtifact memory rawArtifact = abi.decode(parsedData, (RawEIP1559ScriptArtifact));
 380 |     |         EIP1559ScriptArtifact memory artifact;
 381 |     |         artifact.libraries = rawArtifact.libraries;
 382 |     |         artifact.path = rawArtifact.path;
 383 |     |         artifact.timestamp = rawArtifact.timestamp;
 384 |     |         artifact.pending = rawArtifact.pending;
 385 |     |         artifact.txReturns = rawArtifact.txReturns;
 386 |     |         artifact.receipts = rawToConvertedReceipts(rawArtifact.receipts);
 387 |     |         artifact.transactions = rawToConvertedEIPTx1559s(rawArtifact.transactions);
 388 |     |         return artifact;
 389 |     |     }
 390 |     | 
 391 |     |     /// @notice Converts an array of raw EIP-1559 transactions to the user-friendly `Tx1559` format.
 392 |     |     function rawToConvertedEIPTx1559s(RawTx1559[] memory rawTxs) internal pure virtual returns (Tx1559[] memory) {
 393 |     |         Tx1559[] memory txs = new Tx1559[](rawTxs.length);
 394 |     |         for (uint256 i; i < rawTxs.length; i++) {
 395 |     |             txs[i] = rawToConvertedEIPTx1559(rawTxs[i]);
 396 |     |         }
 397 |     |         return txs;
 398 |     |     }
 399 |     | 
 400 |     |     /// @notice Converts a single raw EIP-1559 transaction to the user-friendly `Tx1559` format.
 401 |     |     function rawToConvertedEIPTx1559(RawTx1559 memory rawTx) internal pure virtual returns (Tx1559 memory) {
 402 |     |         Tx1559 memory transaction;
 403 |     |         transaction.arguments = rawTx.arguments;
 404 |     |         transaction.contractAddress = rawTx.contractAddress;
 405 |     |         transaction.contractName = rawTx.contractName;
 406 |     |         transaction.functionSig = rawTx.functionSig;
 407 |     |         transaction.hash = rawTx.hash;
 408 |     |         transaction.txDetail = rawToConvertedEIP1559Detail(rawTx.txDetail);
 409 |     |         transaction.opcode = rawTx.opcode;
 410 |     |         return transaction;
 411 |     |     }
 412 |     | 
 413 |     |     /// @notice Converts raw EIP-1559 transaction detail fields to the user-friendly `Tx1559Detail` format.
 414 |     |     function rawToConvertedEIP1559Detail(RawTx1559Detail memory rawDetail)
 415 |     |         internal
 416 |     |         pure
 417 |     |         virtual
 418 |     |         returns (Tx1559Detail memory)
 419 |     |     {
 420 |     |         Tx1559Detail memory txDetail;
 421 |     |         txDetail.data = rawDetail.data;
 422 |     |         txDetail.from = rawDetail.from;
 423 |     |         txDetail.to = rawDetail.to;
 424 |     |         txDetail.nonce = _bytesToUint(rawDetail.nonce);
 425 |     |         txDetail.txType = _bytesToUint(rawDetail.txType);
 426 |     |         txDetail.value = _bytesToUint(rawDetail.value);
 427 |     |         txDetail.gas = _bytesToUint(rawDetail.gas);
 428 |     |         txDetail.accessList = rawDetail.accessList;
 429 |     |         return txDetail;
 430 |     |     }

 432 |     |     /// @notice Reads all EIP-1559 transactions from the broadcast artifact at `path`.

 436 |     |         RawTx1559[] memory rawTxs = abi.decode(parsedDeployData, (RawTx1559[]));

 440 |     |     /// @notice Reads the EIP-1559 transaction at `index` from the broadcast artifact at `path`.
 441 |     |     function readTx1559(string memory path, uint256 index) internal view virtual returns (Tx1559 memory) {
 442 |     |         string memory deployData = vm.readFile(path);

 444 |     |         bytes memory parsedDeployData = vm.parseJson(deployData, key);

 450 |     |     function readReceipts(string memory path) internal view virtual returns (Receipt[] memory) {
 451 |     |         string memory deployData = vm.readFile(path);
 452 |     |         bytes memory parsedDeployData = vm.parseJson(deployData, ".receipts");
 453 |     |         RawReceipt[] memory rawReceipts = abi.decode(parsedDeployData, (RawReceipt[]));
 454 |     |         return rawToConvertedReceipts(rawReceipts);

 457 |     |     /// @notice Reads the transaction receipt at `index` from the broadcast artifact at `path`.
 458 |     |     function readReceipt(string memory path, uint256 index) internal view virtual returns (Receipt memory) {
 459 |     |         string memory deployData = vm.readFile(path);
 460 |     |         string memory key = string(abi.encodePacked(".receipts[", vm.toString(index), "]"));
 461 |     |         bytes memory parsedDeployData = vm.parseJson(deployData, key);
 462 |     |         RawReceipt memory rawReceipt = abi.decode(parsedDeployData, (RawReceipt));
 463 |     |         return rawToConvertedReceipt(rawReceipt);
 464 |     |     }

 466 |     |     /// @notice Converts an array of raw receipts to the user-friendly `Receipt` format.
 467 |     |     function rawToConvertedReceipts(RawReceipt[] memory rawReceipts) internal pure virtual returns (Receipt[] memory) {
 468 |     |         Receipt[] memory receipts = new Receipt[](rawReceipts.length);
 469 |     |         for (uint256 i; i < rawReceipts.length; i++) {
 470 |     |             receipts[i] = rawToConvertedReceipt(rawReceipts[i]);
 471 |     |         }
 472 |     |         return receipts;
 473 |     |     }
 474 |     | 
 475 |     |     /// @notice Converts a single raw receipt to the user-friendly `Receipt` format.
 476 |     |     function rawToConvertedReceipt(RawReceipt memory rawReceipt) internal pure virtual returns (Receipt memory) {
 477 |     |         Receipt memory receipt;
 478 |     |         receipt.blockHash = rawReceipt.blockHash;
 479 |     |         receipt.to = rawReceipt.to;
 480 |     |         receipt.from = rawReceipt.from;
 481 |     |         receipt.contractAddress = rawReceipt.contractAddress;
 482 |     |         receipt.effectiveGasPrice = _bytesToUint(rawReceipt.effectiveGasPrice);
 483 |     |         receipt.cumulativeGasUsed = _bytesToUint(rawReceipt.cumulativeGasUsed);
 484 |     |         receipt.gasUsed = _bytesToUint(rawReceipt.gasUsed);
 485 |     |         receipt.status = _bytesToUint(rawReceipt.status);
 486 |     |         receipt.transactionIndex = _bytesToUint(rawReceipt.transactionIndex);
 487 |     |         receipt.blockNumber = _bytesToUint(rawReceipt.blockNumber);
 488 |     |         receipt.logs = rawToConvertedReceiptLogs(rawReceipt.logs);
 489 |     |         receipt.logsBloom = rawReceipt.logsBloom;
 490 |     |         receipt.transactionHash = rawReceipt.transactionHash;
 491 |     |         return receipt;
 492 |     |     }
 493 |     | 
 494 |     |     /// @notice Converts an array of raw receipt logs to the user-friendly `ReceiptLog` format.
 495 |     |     function rawToConvertedReceiptLogs(RawReceiptLog[] memory rawLogs)
 496 |     |         internal
 497 |     |         pure
 498 |     |         virtual
 499 |     |         returns (ReceiptLog[] memory)
 500 |     |     {
 501 |     |         ReceiptLog[] memory logs = new ReceiptLog[](rawLogs.length);
 502 |     |         for (uint256 i; i < rawLogs.length; i++) {
 503 |     |             logs[i].logAddress = rawLogs[i].logAddress;
 504 |     |             logs[i].blockHash = rawLogs[i].blockHash;
 505 |     |             logs[i].blockNumber = _bytesToUint(rawLogs[i].blockNumber);
 506 |     |             logs[i].data = rawLogs[i].data;
 507 |     |             logs[i].logIndex = _bytesToUint(rawLogs[i].logIndex);
 508 |     |             logs[i].topics = rawLogs[i].topics;
 509 |     |             logs[i].transactionIndex = _bytesToUint(rawLogs[i].transactionIndex);
 510 |     |             logs[i].transactionLogIndex = _bytesToUint(rawLogs[i].transactionLogIndex);
 511 |     |             logs[i].removed = rawLogs[i].removed;
 512 |     |         }
 513 |     |         return logs;
 514 |     |     }

 556 |     |     /// @notice Creates a labeled address and the corresponding private key derived from `name`.
 557 |     |     function makeAddrAndKey(string memory name) internal virtual returns (address addr, uint256 privateKey) {
 558 |     |         privateKey = uint256(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(name)));

 561 |     |     }

 568 |     |     /// @notice Immediately destroys `who`, zeroing its balance, code, and nonce, and sending its balance to `beneficiary`.
 569 |     |     /// @dev Unlike `selfdestruct`, this takes effect immediately within the same transaction.
 570 |     |     function destroyAccount(address who, address beneficiary) internal virtual {
 571 |     |         uint256 currBalance = who.balance;
 572 |     |         vm.etch(who, abi.encode());
 573 |     |         vm.deal(who, 0);
 574 |     |         vm.resetNonce(who);
 575 |     | 
 576 |     |         uint256 beneficiaryBalance = beneficiary.balance;
 577 |     |         vm.deal(beneficiary, currBalance + beneficiaryBalance);
 578 |     |     }

 581 |     |     function makeAccount(string memory name) internal virtual returns (Account memory account) {
 582 |     |         (account.addr, account.key) = makeAddrAndKey(name);
 583 |     |     }

 588 |     |         virtual

 590 |     |     {

 595 |     |     function _bytesToUint(bytes memory b) private pure returns (uint256) {
 596 |     |         require(b.length <= 32, "StdCheats _bytesToUint(bytes): Bytes length exceeds 32.");
 597 |     |         return abi.decode(abi.encodePacked(new bytes(32 - b.length), b), (uint256));
 598 |     |     }

 621 |     |     /// @notice Disables gas metering for the duration of the function, re-enabling it on exit.
 622 |     |     /// @dev When nested, gas metering is only resumed at the end of the outermost function that uses this modifier.
 623 |     |     modifier noGasMetering() {
 624 |     |         vm.pauseGasMetering();
 625 |     |         // To prevent turning gas monitoring back on with nested functions that use this modifier,
 626 |     |         // we check if gasMetering started in the off position. If it did, we don't want to turn
 627 |     |         // it back on until we exit the top level function that used the modifier
 628 |     |         //
 629 |     |         // i.e. funcA() noGasMetering { funcB() }, where funcB has noGasMetering as well.
 630 |     |         // funcA will have `gasStartedOff` as false, funcB will have it as true,
 631 |     |         // so we only turn metering back on at the end of the funcA
 632 |     |         bool gasStartedOff = _gasMeteringOff;
 633 |     |         _gasMeteringOff = true;
 634 |     | 
 635 |     |         _;
 636 |     | 
 637 |     |         // if gas metering was on when this modifier was called, turn it back on at the end
 638 |     |         if (!gasStartedOff) {
 639 |     |             _gasMeteringOff = false;
 640 |     |             vm.resumeGasMetering();
 641 |     |         }
 642 |     |     }

 644 |     |     // We use this complex approach of `_viewChainId` and `_pureChainId` to ensure there are no
 645 |     |     // compiler warnings when accessing chain ID in any solidity version supported by forge-std. We
 646 |     |     // can't simply access the chain ID in a normal view or pure function because the solc View Pure
 647 |     |     // Checker changed `chainid` from pure to view in 0.8.0.
 648 |     |     function _viewChainId() private view returns (uint256 chainId) {
 649 |     |         // Assembly required since `block.chainid` was introduced in 0.8.0.
 650 |     |         assembly {
 651 |     |             chainId := chainid()
 652 |     |         }
 653 |     | 
 654 |     |         address(this); // Silence warnings in older Solc versions.
 655 |     |     }
 656 |     | 
 657 |     |     function _pureChainId() private pure returns (uint256 chainId) {
 658 |     |         function() internal view returns (uint256) fnIn = _viewChainId;
 659 |     |         function() internal pure returns (uint256) pureChainId;
 660 |     |         assembly {
 661 |     |             pureChainId := fnIn
 662 |     |         }
 663 |     |         chainId = pureChainId();
 664 |     |     }
 665 |     | }

 824 |     |     /// @notice Sets the ERC20 `token` balance of `to` to `give`, optionally adjusting the total supply.
 825 |     |     function deal(address token, address to, uint256 give, bool adjust) internal virtual {
 826 |     |         // get current balance
 827 |     |         (, bytes memory balData) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(0x70a08231, to));
 828 |     |         uint256 prevBal = abi.decode(balData, (uint256));
 829 |     | 
 830 |     |         // update balance
 831 |     |         _stdstore.target(token).sig(0x70a08231).with_key(to).checked_write(give);
 832 |     | 
 833 |     |         // update total supply
 834 |     |         if (adjust) {
 835 |     |             (, bytes memory totSupData) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(0x18160ddd));
 836 |     |             uint256 totSup = abi.decode(totSupData, (uint256));
 837 |     |             if (give < prevBal) {
 838 |     |                 totSup -= (prevBal - give);
 839 |     |             } else {
 840 |     |                 totSup += (give - prevBal);
 841 |     |             }
 842 |     |             _stdstore.target(token).sig(0x18160ddd).checked_write(totSup);
 843 |     |         }
 844 |     |     }
 845 |     | 
 846 |     |     /// @notice Sets the ERC1155 `token` balance of `to` for token `id` to `give`, optionally adjusting the total supply.
 847 |     |     function dealERC1155(address token, address to, uint256 id, uint256 give, bool adjust) internal virtual {
 848 |     |         // get current balance
 849 |     |         (, bytes memory balData) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(0x00fdd58e, to, id));
 850 |     |         uint256 prevBal = abi.decode(balData, (uint256));
 851 |     | 
 852 |     |         // update balance
 853 |     |         _stdstore.target(token).sig(0x00fdd58e).with_key(to).with_key(id).checked_write(give);
 854 |     | 
 855 |     |         // update total supply
 856 |     |         if (adjust) {
 857 |     |             (, bytes memory totSupData) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(0xbd85b039, id));
 858 |     |             require(
 859 |     |                 totSupData.length != 0,
 860 |     |                 "StdCheats dealERC1155(address,address,uint256,uint256,bool): target contract is not ERC1155Supply."
 861 |     |             );
 862 |     |             uint256 totSup = abi.decode(totSupData, (uint256));
 863 |     |             if (give < prevBal) {
 864 |     |                 totSup -= (prevBal - give);
 865 |     |             } else {
 866 |     |                 totSup += (give - prevBal);
 867 |     |             }
 868 |     |             _stdstore.target(token).sig(0xbd85b039).with_key(id).checked_write(totSup);
 869 |     |         }
 870 |     |     }

 872 |     |     /// @notice Transfers ownership of ERC721 `token` with `id` to `to`, updating balances accordingly.
 873 |     |     function dealERC721(address token, address to, uint256 id) internal virtual {
 874 |     |         // check if token id is already minted and the actual owner.
 875 |     |         (bool successMinted, bytes memory ownerData) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(0x6352211e, id));
 876 |     |         require(successMinted, "StdCheats dealERC721(address,address,uint256): id not minted.");
 877 |     | 
 878 |     |         // get owner current balance
 879 |     |         (, bytes memory fromBalData) =
 880 |     |             token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(0x70a08231, abi.decode(ownerData, (address))));
 881 |     |         uint256 fromPrevBal = abi.decode(fromBalData, (uint256));
 882 |     | 
 883 |     |         // get new user current balance
 884 |     |         (, bytes memory toBalData) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(0x70a08231, to));
 885 |     |         uint256 toPrevBal = abi.decode(toBalData, (uint256));
 886 |     | 
 887 |     |         // update balances
 888 |     |         _stdstore.target(token).sig(0x70a08231).with_key(abi.decode(ownerData, (address))).checked_write(--fromPrevBal);
 889 |     |         _stdstore.target(token).sig(0x70a08231).with_key(to).checked_write(++toPrevBal);
 890 |     | 
 891 |     |         // update owner
 892 |     |         _stdstore.target(token).sig(0x6352211e).with_key(id).checked_write(to);
 893 |     |     }

 907 |     |     /// @notice Etches the runtime bytecode of `what` (from the artifacts directory) at `where`, using `args` as ABI-encoded constructor arguments and sending `value` wei to the constructor.
 908 |     |     /// @dev Runs the contract's creation code via `vm.etch` + a self-call, then etches the resulting runtime code at `where`. Constructor side-effects on other contracts are not preserved.
 909 |     |     function deployCodeTo(string memory what, bytes memory args, uint256 value, address where) internal virtual {
 910 |     |         bytes memory creationCode = vm.getCode(what);
 911 |     |         vm.etch(where, abi.encodePacked(creationCode, args));

 913 |     |         require(success, "StdCheats deployCodeTo(string,bytes,uint256,address): Failed to create runtime bytecode.");
 914 |     |         vm.etch(where, runtimeBytecode);
 915 |     |     }

   7 |     | // `key` parameters use the same selector syntax as the `vm.parseJson*` cheatcodes,
   8 |     | // for example `.a` for a nested field or `$` for the root object.
   9 |     | // To parse:
  10 |     | // ```
  11 |     | // using stdJson for string;
  12 |     | // string memory json = vm.readFile("<some_path>");
  13 |     | // uint256 value = json.readUint(".a");
  14 |     | // bytes memory encoded = json.parseRaw("$");
  15 |     | // ```
  16 |     | // To write:
  17 |     | // ```
  18 |     | // using stdJson for string;
  19 |     | // string memory json = "json";
  20 |     | // json.serialize("a", uint256(123));
  21 |     | // string memory semiFinal = json.serialize("b", string("test"));
  22 |     | // string memory finalJson = json.serialize("c", semiFinal);
  23 |     | // finalJson.write("<some_path>");

  1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0
  2 |     | pragma solidity >=0.8.13 <0.9.0;
  3 |     | 
  4 |     | /// @notice Mathematical utility functions for unsigned and signed integers.
  5 |     | library stdMath {
  6 |     |     int256 private constant _INT256_MIN =
  7 |     |         -57896044618658097711785492504343953926634992332820282019728792003956564819968;
  8 |     | 
  9 |     |     /// @notice Computes the absolute value of a signed integer.
 10 |     |     /// @param a The signed integer to compute the absolute value of.
 11 |     |     /// @return The absolute value as an unsigned integer.
 12 |     |     function abs(int256 a) internal pure returns (uint256) {
 13 |     |         // Required or it will fail when `a = type(int256).min`
 14 |     |         if (a == _INT256_MIN) {
 15 |     |             return 57896044618658097711785492504343953926634992332820282019728792003956564819968;
 16 |     |         }
 17 |     | 
 18 |     |         return uint256(a > 0 ? a : -a);
 19 |     |     }
 20 |     | 
 21 |     |     /// @notice Computes the absolute difference between two unsigned integers.
 22 |     |     /// @param a The first unsigned integer.
 23 |     |     /// @param b The second unsigned integer.
 24 |     |     /// @return The absolute difference between `a` and `b`.
 25 |     |     function delta(uint256 a, uint256 b) internal pure returns (uint256) {
 26 |     |         return a > b ? a - b : b - a;
 27 |     |     }
 28 |     | 
 29 |     |     /// @notice Computes the absolute difference between two signed integers.
 30 |     |     /// @param a The first signed integer.
 31 |     |     /// @param b The second signed integer.
 32 |     |     /// @return The absolute difference between `a` and `b`.
 33 |     |     function delta(int256 a, int256 b) internal pure returns (uint256) {
 34 |     |         // a and b are of the same sign
 35 |     |         // this works thanks to two's complement, the left-most bit is the sign bit
 36 |     |         if ((a ^ b) > -1) {
 37 |     |             return delta(abs(a), abs(b));
 38 |     |         }
 39 |     | 
 40 |     |         // a and b are of opposite signs
 41 |     |         return abs(a) + abs(b);
 42 |     |     }
 43 |     | 
 44 |     |     /// @notice Computes the percentage difference between two unsigned integers, scaled by 1e18.
 45 |     |     /// @param a The value to compare.
 46 |     |     /// @param b The reference value (divisor). Must not be zero.
 47 |     |     /// @return The percentage difference scaled by 1e18 (1e18 represents 100%).
 48 |     |     function percentDelta(uint256 a, uint256 b) internal pure returns (uint256) {
 49 |     |         // Prevent division by zero
 50 |     |         require(b != 0, "stdMath percentDelta(uint256,uint256): Divisor is zero");
 51 |     |         uint256 absDelta = delta(a, b);
 52 |     | 
 53 |     |         return absDelta * 1e18 / b;
 54 |     |     }
 55 |     | 
 56 |     |     /// @notice Computes the percentage difference between two signed integers, scaled by 1e18.
 57 |     |     /// @param a The value to compare.
 58 |     |     /// @param b The reference value (divisor). Its absolute value must not be zero.
 59 |     |     /// @return The percentage difference scaled by 1e18 (1e18 represents 100%).
 60 |     |     function percentDelta(int256 a, int256 b) internal pure returns (uint256) {
 61 |     |         uint256 absDelta = delta(a, b);
 62 |     |         uint256 absB = abs(b);
 63 |     |         // Prevent division by zero
 64 |     |         require(absB != 0, "stdMath percentDelta(int256,int256): Divisor is zero");
 65 |     | 
 66 |     |         return absDelta * 1e18 / absB;
 67 |     |     }
 68 |     | }

/home/redkidd/SoloTime/HedgeyFund/valari/valari-contracts/lib/forge-std/src/StdStorage.sol
   1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0
   2 |     | pragma solidity >=0.8.13 <0.9.0;
   3 |     | 
   4 |     | import {Vm} from "./Vm.sol";
   5 |     | 
   6 |     | struct FindData {
   7 |     |     uint256 slot;
   8 |     |     uint256 offsetLeft;
   9 |     |     uint256 offsetRight;
  10 |     |     bool found;
  11 |     | }
  12 |     | 
  13 |     | struct StdStorage {
  14 |     |     mapping(address => mapping(bytes4 => mapping(bytes32 => FindData))) finds;
  15 |     |     bytes32[] _keys;
  16 |     |     bytes4 _sig;
  17 |     |     uint256 _depth;
  18 |     |     address _target;
  19 |     |     bytes32 _set;
  20 |     |     bool _enable_packed_slots;
  21 |     |     bytes _calldata;
  22 |     | }
  23 |     | 
  24 |     | library stdStorageSafe {
  25 |     |     event SlotFound(address who, bytes4 fsig, bytes32 keysHash, uint256 slot);
  26 |     |     event WARNING_UninitedSlot(address who, uint256 slot);
  27 |     | 
  28 |     |     Vm private constant vm = Vm(address(uint160(uint256(keccak256("hevm cheat code")))));
  29 |     |     uint256 constant UINT256_MAX = 115792089237316195423570985008687907853269984665640564039457584007913129639935;
  30 |     | 
  31 |     |     /// @notice Returns the 4-byte function selector for `sigStr`.
  32 |     |     function sigs(string memory sigStr) internal pure returns (bytes4) {
  33 |     |         return bytes4(keccak256(bytes(sigStr)));
  34 |     |     }
  35 |     | 
  36 |     |     /// @notice Returns the encoded call parameters (keys or raw calldata) for the configured target function.
  37 |     |     function getCallParams(StdStorage storage self) internal view returns (bytes memory) {
  38 |     |         if (self._calldata.length == 0) {
  39 |     |             return _flatten(self._keys);
  40 |     |         } else {
  41 |     |             return self._calldata;
  42 |     |         }
  43 |     |     }
  44 |     | 
  45 |     |     /// @notice Calls the target contract with the configured parameters and returns the success flag and return value.
  46 |     |     function callTarget(StdStorage storage self) internal view returns (bool, bytes32) {
  47 |     |         bytes memory cd = abi.encodePacked(self._sig, getCallParams(self));
  48 |     |         (bool success, bytes memory rdat) = self._target.staticcall(cd);
  49 |     |         bytes32 result = _bytesToBytes32(rdat, 32 * self._depth);
  50 |     | 
  51 |     |         return (success, result);
  52 |     |     }
  53 |     | 
  54 |     |     /// @notice Returns whether mutating `slot` changes the return value of the configured target call.
  55 |     |     /// @dev Temporarily writes either `type(uint256).max` or `0` to the slot to detect sensitivity.
  56 |     |     function checkSlotMutatesCall(StdStorage storage self, bytes32 slot) internal returns (bool) {
  57 |     |         bytes32 prevSlotValue = vm.load(self._target, slot);
  58 |     |         (bool success, bytes32 prevReturnValue) = callTarget(self);
  59 |     | 
  60 |     |         bytes32 testVal = prevReturnValue == bytes32(0) ? bytes32(UINT256_MAX) : bytes32(0);
  61 |     |         vm.store(self._target, slot, testVal);
  62 |     | 
  63 |     |         (, bytes32 newReturnValue) = callTarget(self);
  64 |     | 
  65 |     |         vm.store(self._target, slot, prevSlotValue);
  66 |     | 
  67 |     |         return (success && (prevReturnValue != newReturnValue));
  68 |     |     }
  69 |     | 
  70 |     |     /// @notice Searches for the bit offset of the packed variable within `slot` from the left or right side.
  71 |     |     function findOffset(StdStorage storage self, bytes32 slot, bool left) internal returns (bool, uint256) {
  72 |     |         for (uint256 offset = 0; offset < 256; offset++) {
  73 |     |             uint256 valueToPut = left ? (1 << (255 - offset)) : (1 << offset);
  74 |     |             vm.store(self._target, slot, bytes32(valueToPut));
  75 |     | 
  76 |     |             (bool success, bytes32 data) = callTarget(self);
  77 |     | 
  78 |     |             if (success && (uint256(data) > 0)) {
  79 |     |                 return (true, offset);
  80 |     |             }
  81 |     |         }
  82 |     |         return (false, 0);
  83 |     |     }
  84 |     | 
  85 |     |     /// @notice Returns whether both offsets were found, along with the left and right bit offsets of the packed variable within `slot`.
  86 |     |     function findOffsets(StdStorage storage self, bytes32 slot) internal returns (bool, uint256, uint256) {
  87 |     |         bytes32 prevSlotValue = vm.load(self._target, slot);
  88 |     | 
  89 |     |         (bool foundLeft, uint256 offsetLeft) = findOffset(self, slot, true);
  90 |     |         (bool foundRight, uint256 offsetRight) = findOffset(self, slot, false);
  91 |     | 
  92 |     |         // `findOffset` may mutate slot value, so we are setting it to initial value
  93 |     |         vm.store(self._target, slot, prevSlotValue);
  94 |     |         return (foundLeft && foundRight, offsetLeft, offsetRight);
  95 |     |     }
  96 |     | 
  97 |     |     /// @notice Finds the storage slot for the configured target and returns its data, clearing the configuration.
  98 |     |     function find(StdStorage storage self) internal returns (FindData storage) {
  99 |     |         return find(self, true);
 100 |     |     }
 101 |     | 
 102 |     |     /// @notice find an arbitrary storage slot given a function sig, input data, address of the contract and a value to check against
 103 |     |     // slot complexity:
 104 |     |     //  if flat, will be bytes32(uint256(uint));
 105 |     |     //  if map, will be keccak256(abi.encode(key, uint(slot)));
 106 |     |     //  if deep map, will be keccak256(abi.encode(key1, keccak256(abi.encode(key0, uint(slot)))));
 107 |     |     //  if map struct, will be bytes32(uint256(keccak256(abi.encode(key1, keccak256(abi.encode(key0, uint(slot)))))) + structFieldDepth);
 108 |     |     function find(StdStorage storage self, bool _clear) internal returns (FindData storage) {
 109 |     |         address who = self._target;
 110 |     |         bytes4 fsig = self._sig;
 111 |     |         uint256 field_depth = self._depth;
 112 |     |         bytes memory params = getCallParams(self);
 113 |     | 
 114 |     |         // calldata to test against
 115 |     |         if (self.finds[who][fsig][keccak256(abi.encodePacked(params, field_depth))].found) {
 116 |     |             if (_clear) {
 117 |     |                 clear(self);
 118 |     |             }
 119 |     |             return self.finds[who][fsig][keccak256(abi.encodePacked(params, field_depth))];
 120 |     |         }
 121 |     |         vm.record();
 122 |     |         (, bytes32 callResult) = callTarget(self);
 123 |     |         (bytes32[] memory reads,) = vm.accesses(address(who));
 124 |     | 
 125 |     |         if (reads.length == 0) {
 126 |     |             revert("stdStorage find(StdStorage): No storage use detected for target.");
 127 |     |         } else {
 128 |     |             for (uint256 i = reads.length; i > 0;) {
 129 |     |                 --i;
 130 |     |                 bytes32 prev = vm.load(who, reads[i]);
 131 |     |                 if (prev == bytes32(0)) {
 132 |     |                     emit WARNING_UninitedSlot(who, uint256(reads[i]));
 133 |     |                 }
 134 |     | 
 135 |     |                 if (!checkSlotMutatesCall(self, reads[i])) {
 136 |     |                     continue;
 137 |     |                 }
 138 |     | 
 139 |     |                 (uint256 offsetLeft, uint256 offsetRight) = (0, 0);
 140 |     | 
 141 |     |                 if (self._enable_packed_slots) {
 142 |     |                     bool found;
 143 |     |                     (found, offsetLeft, offsetRight) = findOffsets(self, reads[i]);
 144 |     |                     if (!found) {
 145 |     |                         continue;
 146 |     |                     }
 147 |     |                 }
 148 |     | 
 149 |     |                 // Check that value between found offsets is equal to the current call result
 150 |     |                 uint256 curVal = (uint256(prev) & getMaskByOffsets(offsetLeft, offsetRight)) >> offsetRight;
 151 |     | 
 152 |     |                 if (uint256(callResult) != curVal) {
 153 |     |                     continue;
 154 |     |                 }
 155 |     | 
 156 |     |                 emit SlotFound(who, fsig, keccak256(abi.encodePacked(params, field_depth)), uint256(reads[i]));
 157 |     |                 self.finds[who][fsig][keccak256(abi.encodePacked(params, field_depth))] =
 158 |     |                     FindData(uint256(reads[i]), offsetLeft, offsetRight, true);
 159 |     |                 break;
 160 |     |             }
 161 |     |         }
 162 |     | 
 163 |     |         require(
 164 |     |             self.finds[who][fsig][keccak256(abi.encodePacked(params, field_depth))].found,
 165 |     |             "stdStorage find(StdStorage): Slot(s) not found."
 166 |     |         );
 167 |     | 
 168 |     |         if (_clear) {
 169 |     |             clear(self);
 170 |     |         }
 171 |     |         return self.finds[who][fsig][keccak256(abi.encodePacked(params, field_depth))];
 172 |     |     }
 173 |     | 
 174 |     |     /// @notice Sets the target contract address for the storage lookup.
 175 |     |     function target(StdStorage storage self, address _target) internal returns (StdStorage storage) {
 176 |     |         self._target = _target;
 177 |     |         return self;
 178 |     |     }
 179 |     | 
 180 |     |     /// @notice Sets the target function selector for the storage lookup.
 181 |     |     function sig(StdStorage storage self, bytes4 _sig) internal returns (StdStorage storage) {
 182 |     |         self._sig = _sig;

 265 |     |     /// @notice Returns the parent mapping slot index and the key used to reach the found slot.
 266 |     |     function parent(StdStorage storage self) internal returns (uint256, bytes32) {
 267 |     |         address who = self._target;
 268 |     |         uint256 field_depth = self._depth;
 269 |     |         vm.startMappingRecording();
 270 |     |         uint256 child = find(self, true).slot - field_depth;
 271 |     |         (bool found, bytes32 key, bytes32 parent_slot) = vm.getMappingKeyAndParentOf(who, bytes32(child));
 272 |     |         if (!found) {
 273 |     |             revert(
 274 |     |                 "stdStorage parent(StdStorage): Cannot find parent. Make sure you give a slot and startMappingRecording() has been called."
 275 |     |             );
 276 |     |         }
 277 |     |         return (uint256(parent_slot), key);
 278 |     |     }
 279 |     | 
 280 |     |     /// @notice Returns the root mapping slot index by traversing the mapping parent chain.
 281 |     |     function root(StdStorage storage self) internal returns (uint256) {
 282 |     |         address who = self._target;
 283 |     |         uint256 field_depth = self._depth;
 284 |     |         vm.startMappingRecording();
 285 |     |         uint256 child = find(self, true).slot - field_depth;
 286 |     |         bool found;
 287 |     |         bytes32 root_slot;
 288 |     |         bytes32 parent_slot;
 289 |     |         (found,, parent_slot) = vm.getMappingKeyAndParentOf(who, bytes32(child));
 290 |     |         if (!found) {
 291 |     |             revert(
 292 |     |                 "stdStorage root(StdStorage): Cannot find parent. Make sure you give a slot and startMappingRecording() has been called."
 293 |     |             );
 294 |     |         }
 295 |     |         while (found) {
 296 |     |             root_slot = parent_slot;
 297 |     |             (found,, parent_slot) = vm.getMappingKeyAndParentOf(who, bytes32(root_slot));
 298 |     |         }
 299 |     |         return uint256(root_slot);
 300 |     |     }
 301 |     | 
 302 |     |     function _bytesToBytes32(bytes memory b, uint256 offset) private pure returns (bytes32) {
 303 |     |         bytes32 out;
 304 |     | 
 305 |     |         // Cap read length by remaining bytes from `offset`, and at most 32 bytes to avoid out-of-bounds
 306 |     |         uint256 max = b.length > offset ? b.length - offset : 0;
 307 |     |         if (max > 32) {
 308 |     |             max = 32;
 309 |     |         }
 310 |     |         for (uint256 i = 0; i < max; i++) {
 311 |     |             out |= bytes32(b[offset + i] & 0xFF) >> (i * 8);
 312 |     |         }
 313 |     |         return out;
 314 |     |     }
 315 |     | 
 316 |     |     function _flatten(bytes32[] memory b) private pure returns (bytes memory) {
 317 |     |         bytes memory result = new bytes(b.length * 32);
 318 |     |         for (uint256 i = 0; i < b.length; i++) {
 319 |     |             bytes32 k = b[i];
 320 |     |             assembly ("memory-safe") {
 321 |     |                 mstore(add(result, add(32, mul(32, i))), k)
 322 |     |             }
 323 |     |         }
 324 |     | 
 325 |     |         return result;
 326 |     |     }

 328 |     |     /// @notice Resets all configured parameters on `self`.
 329 |     |     function clear(StdStorage storage self) internal {
 330 |     |         delete self._target;
 331 |     |         delete self._sig;
 332 |     |         delete self._keys;
 333 |     |         delete self._depth;
 334 |     |         delete self._enable_packed_slots;
 335 |     |         delete self._calldata;
 336 |     |     }
 337 |     | 
 338 |     |     /// @notice Returns a bitmask with ones in the bit range `[offsetRight, 255 - offsetLeft]`.
 339 |     |     /// @dev `(slotValue & mask) >> offsetRight` extracts the packed variable's value.
 340 |     |     function getMaskByOffsets(uint256 offsetLeft, uint256 offsetRight) internal pure returns (uint256 mask) {
 341 |     |         // mask = ((1 << (256 - (offsetRight + offsetLeft))) - 1) << offsetRight;
 342 |     |         // using assembly because (1 << 256) causes overflow
 343 |     |         assembly {
 344 |     |             mask := shl(offsetRight, sub(shl(sub(256, add(offsetRight, offsetLeft)), 1), 1))
 345 |     |         }
 346 |     |     }
 347 |     | 
 348 |     |     /// @notice Returns `curValue` with the packed variable at `[offsetRight, 255 - offsetLeft]` replaced by `varValue`.
 349 |     |     function getUpdatedSlotValue(bytes32 curValue, uint256 varValue, uint256 offsetLeft, uint256 offsetRight)
 350 |     |         internal
 351 |     |         pure
 352 |     |         returns (bytes32 newValue)
 353 |     |     {
 354 |     |         return bytes32((uint256(curValue) & ~getMaskByOffsets(offsetLeft, offsetRight)) | (varValue << offsetRight));
 355 |     |     }

 442 |     |     function checked_write(StdStorage storage self, bool write) internal {
 443 |     |         bytes32 t;
 444 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {

 446 |     |         }
 447 |     |         checked_write(self, t);
 448 |     |     }

 450 |     |     /// @notice Writes `set` to the found storage slot and verifies the value was applied correctly.
 451 |     |     function checked_write(StdStorage storage self, bytes32 set) internal {
 452 |     |         address who = self._target;
 453 |     |         bytes4 fsig = self._sig;
 454 |     |         uint256 field_depth = self._depth;
 455 |     |         bytes memory params = stdStorageSafe.getCallParams(self);
 456 |     | 
 457 |     |         if (!self.finds[who][fsig][keccak256(abi.encodePacked(params, field_depth))].found) {
 458 |     |             find(self, false);
 459 |     |         }
 460 |     |         FindData storage data = self.finds[who][fsig][keccak256(abi.encodePacked(params, field_depth))];
 461 |     |         if ((data.offsetLeft + data.offsetRight) > 0) {
 462 |     |             uint256 maxVal = 2 ** (256 - (data.offsetLeft + data.offsetRight));
 463 |     |             require(
 464 |     |                 uint256(set) < maxVal,
 465 |     |                 string(
 466 |     |                     abi.encodePacked(
 467 |     |                         "stdStorage checked_write(StdStorage): Packed slot. We can't fit value greater than ",
 468 |     |                         vm.toString(maxVal)
 469 |     |                     )
 470 |     |                 )
 471 |     |             );
 472 |     |         }
 473 |     |         bytes32 curVal = vm.load(who, bytes32(data.slot));
 474 |     |         bytes32 valToSet = stdStorageSafe.getUpdatedSlotValue(curVal, uint256(set), data.offsetLeft, data.offsetRight);
 475 |     | 
 476 |     |         vm.store(who, bytes32(data.slot), valToSet);
 477 |     | 
 478 |     |         (bool success, bytes32 callResult) = stdStorageSafe.callTarget(self);
 479 |     | 
 480 |     |         if (!success || callResult != set) {
 481 |     |             vm.store(who, bytes32(data.slot), curVal);
 482 |     |             revert("stdStorage checked_write(StdStorage): Failed to write value.");
 483 |     |         }
 484 |     |         clear(self);
 485 |     |     }

  14 |     |     address private constant _CONSOLE2_ADDRESS = 0x000000000000000000636F6e736F6c652e6c6f67;
  15 |     |     uint256 private constant _INT256_MIN_ABS =
  16 |     |         57896044618658097711785492504343953926634992332820282019728792003956564819968;
  17 |     |     uint256 private constant _SECP256K1_ORDER =
  18 |     |         115792089237316195423570985008687907852837564279074904382605163141518161494337;
  19 |     |     uint256 private constant _UINT256_MAX =
  20 |     |         115792089237316195423570985008687907853269984665640564039457584007913129639935;
  21 |     | 
  22 |     |     /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
  23 |     |                                  INTERNAL FUNCTIONS
  24 |     |     //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/
  25 |     | 
  26 |     |     /// @notice Maps an unsigned integer into the inclusive range `[min, max]`.
  27 |     |     /// @dev Values outside the range are wrapped into it.
  28 |     |     /// @param x The unsigned value to bound.
  29 |     |     /// @param min The inclusive lower bound.
  30 |     |     /// @param max The inclusive upper bound.
  31 |     |     /// @return result The bounded value.
  32 |     |     function _bound(uint256 x, uint256 min, uint256 max) internal pure virtual returns (uint256 result) {
  33 |     |         require(min <= max, "StdUtils bound(uint256,uint256,uint256): Max is less than min.");
  34 |     |         // If x is between min and max, return x directly. This is to ensure that dictionary values
  35 |     |         // do not get shifted if the min is nonzero. More info: https://github.com/foundry-rs/forge-std/issues/188
  36 |     |         if (x >= min && x <= max) return x;
  37 |     | 
  38 |     |         uint256 size = max - min + 1;
  39 |     | 
  40 |     |         // If the value is 0, 1, 2, 3, wrap that to min, min+1, min+2, min+3. Similarly for the _UINT256_MAX side.
  41 |     |         // This helps ensure coverage of the min/max values.
  42 |     |         if (x <= 3 && size > x) return min + x;
  43 |     |         if (x >= _UINT256_MAX - 3 && size > _UINT256_MAX - x) return max - (_UINT256_MAX - x);
  44 |     | 
  45 |     |         // Otherwise, wrap x into the range [min, max], i.e. the range is inclusive.
  46 |     |         if (x > max) {
  47 |     |             uint256 diff = x - max;
  48 |     |             uint256 rem = diff % size;
  49 |     |             if (rem == 0) return max;
  50 |     |             result = min + rem - 1;
  51 |     |         } else if (x < min) {
  52 |     |             uint256 diff = min - x;
  53 |     |             uint256 rem = diff % size;
  54 |     |             if (rem == 0) return min;
  55 |     |             result = max - rem + 1;
  56 |     |         }
  57 |     |     }
  58 |     | 
  59 |     |     /// @notice Wrapper for `_bound(uint256,uint256,uint256)`.
  60 |     |     /// @param x The unsigned value to bound.
  61 |     |     /// @param min The inclusive lower bound.
  62 |     |     /// @param max The inclusive upper bound.
  63 |     |     /// @return result The bounded value.
  64 |     |     function bound(uint256 x, uint256 min, uint256 max) internal pure virtual returns (uint256 result) {
  65 |     |         result = _bound(x, min, max);
  66 |     |     }
  67 |     | 
  68 |     |     /// @notice Maps a signed integer into the inclusive range `[min, max]`.
  69 |     |     /// @dev Values outside the range are wrapped into it.
  70 |     |     /// @param x The signed value to bound.
  71 |     |     /// @param min The inclusive lower bound.
  72 |     |     /// @param max The inclusive upper bound.
  73 |     |     /// @return result The bounded value.
  74 |     |     function _bound(int256 x, int256 min, int256 max) internal pure virtual returns (int256 result) {
  75 |     |         require(min <= max, "StdUtils bound(int256,int256,int256): Max is less than min.");
  76 |     | 
  77 |     |         // Shifting all int256 values to uint256 to use _bound function. The range of two types are:
  78 |     |         // int256 : -(2**255) ~ (2**255 - 1)
  79 |     |         // uint256:     0     ~ (2**256 - 1)
  80 |     |         // So, add 2**255, _INT256_MIN_ABS to the integer values.
  81 |     |         //
  82 |     |         // If the given integer value is -2**255, we cannot use `-uint256(-x)` because of the overflow.
  83 |     |         // So, use `~uint256(x) + 1` instead.
  84 |     |         uint256 _x = x < 0 ? (_INT256_MIN_ABS - ~uint256(x) - 1) : (uint256(x) + _INT256_MIN_ABS);
  85 |     |         uint256 _min = min < 0 ? (_INT256_MIN_ABS - ~uint256(min) - 1) : (uint256(min) + _INT256_MIN_ABS);
  86 |     |         uint256 _max = max < 0 ? (_INT256_MIN_ABS - ~uint256(max) - 1) : (uint256(max) + _INT256_MIN_ABS);
  87 |     | 
  88 |     |         uint256 y = _bound(_x, _min, _max);
  89 |     | 
  90 |     |         // To move it back to int256 value, subtract _INT256_MIN_ABS at here.
  91 |     |         result = y < _INT256_MIN_ABS ? int256(~(_INT256_MIN_ABS - y) + 1) : int256(y - _INT256_MIN_ABS);
  92 |     |     }
  93 |     | 
  94 |     |     /// @notice Wrapper for `_bound(int256,int256,int256)`.
  95 |     |     /// @param x The signed value to bound.
  96 |     |     /// @param min The inclusive lower bound.
  97 |     |     /// @param max The inclusive upper bound.
  98 |     |     /// @return result The bounded value.
  99 |     |     function bound(int256 x, int256 min, int256 max) internal pure virtual returns (int256 result) {
 100 |     |         result = _bound(x, min, max);
 101 |     |     }

 169 |     |     /// @notice Queries ERC-20 balances for multiple addresses in one Multicall3 request.
 170 |     |     /// @param token The ERC-20 token contract to query.
 171 |     |     /// @param addresses The addresses to query balances for.
 172 |     |     /// @return balances The token balances in the same order as `addresses`.
 173 |     |     function getTokenBalances(address token, address[] memory addresses)
 174 |     |         internal
 175 |     |         virtual
 176 |     |         returns (uint256[] memory balances)
 177 |     |     {
 178 |     |         uint256 tokenCodeSize;
 179 |     |         assembly {
 180 |     |             tokenCodeSize := extcodesize(token)
 181 |     |         }
 182 |     |         require(tokenCodeSize > 0, "StdUtils getTokenBalances(address,address[]): Token address is not a contract.");
 183 |     | 
 184 |     |         // ABI encode the aggregate call to Multicall3.
 185 |     |         uint256 length = addresses.length;
 186 |     |         IMulticall3.Call[] memory calls = new IMulticall3.Call[](length);
 187 |     |         for (uint256 i = 0; i < length; ++i) {
 188 |     |             // 0x70a08231 = bytes4(keccak256("balanceOf(address)"))
 189 |     |             calls[i] = IMulticall3.Call({target: token, callData: abi.encodeWithSelector(0x70a08231, (addresses[i]))});
 190 |     |         }
 191 |     | 
 192 |     |         // Make the aggregate call.
 193 |     |         (, bytes[] memory returnData) = StdConstants.MULTICALL3_ADDRESS.aggregate(calls);
 194 |     | 
 195 |     |         // ABI decode the return data and return the balances.
 196 |     |         balances = new uint256[](length);
 197 |     |         for (uint256 i = 0; i < length; ++i) {
 198 |     |             balances[i] = abi.decode(returnData[i], (uint256));
 199 |     |         }
 200 |     |     }

 210 |     |     // This section is used to prevent the compilation of console, which shortens the compilation time when console is
 211 |     |     // not used elsewhere. We also trick the compiler into letting us make the console log methods as `pure` to avoid
 212 |     |     // any breaking changes to function signatures.
 213 |     |     function _castLogPayloadViewToPure(function(bytes memory) internal view fnIn)
 214 |     |         internal
 215 |     |         pure
 216 |     |         returns (function(bytes memory) internal pure fnOut)
 217 |     |     {
 218 |     |         assembly {
 219 |     |             fnOut := fnIn
 220 |     |         }
 221 |     |     }
 222 |     | 
 223 |     |     function _sendLogPayload(bytes memory payload) internal pure {
 224 |     |         _castLogPayloadViewToPure(_sendLogPayloadView)(payload);
 225 |     |     }
 226 |     | 
 227 |     |     function _sendLogPayloadView(bytes memory payload) private view {
 228 |     |         uint256 payloadLength = payload.length;
 229 |     |         address consoleAddress = _CONSOLE2_ADDRESS;
 230 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 231 |     |             let payloadStart := add(payload, 32)
 232 |     |             let r := staticcall(gas(), consoleAddress, payloadStart, payloadLength, 0, 0)
 233 |     |         }
 234 |     |     }
 235 |     | 
 236 |     |     function _console2_log_StdUtils(string memory p0) private pure {
 237 |     |         _sendLogPayload(abi.encodeWithSignature("log(string)", p0));
 238 |     |     }

 240 |     |     function _console2_log_StdUtils(string memory p0, uint256 p1) private pure {
 241 |     |         _sendLogPayload(abi.encodeWithSignature("log(string,uint256)", p0, p1));
 242 |     |     }

  464 |     |     /// if `--sender` is not provided and not exactly one signer is passed to the script.

 2049 |     | /// The `Vm` interface does allow manipulation of the EVM state. These are all intended to be used

 2066 |     |     /// Sets the blobhashes in the transaction.

 2070 |     | 
 2071 |     |     /// Sets `block.chainid`.

    10 |     |     // for the view-to-pure log trick.

    18 |     |     }

    21 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {

    45 |     |             bytes32 m1;
    46 |     |             bytes32 m2;

    49 |     |                 m1 := mload(sub(offset, 0x40))

  6 |     | /**
  7 |     |  * @dev Interface of the ERC20 standard as defined in the EIP.
  8 |     |  */
  9 |     | interface IERC20 {
 10 |     |     /**
 11 |     |      * @dev Emitted when `value` tokens are moved from one account (`from`) to
 12 |     |      * another (`to`).
 13 |     |      *
 14 |     |      * Note that `value` may be zero.
 15 |     |      */
 16 |     |     event Transfer(address indexed from, address indexed to, uint256 value);
 17 |     | 
 18 |     |     /**
 19 |     |      * @dev Emitted when the allowance of a `spender` for an `owner` is set by
 20 |     |      * a call to {approve}. `value` is the new allowance.
 21 |     |      */
 22 |     |     event Approval(address indexed owner, address indexed spender, uint256 value);
 23 |     | 
 24 |     |     /**
 25 |     |      * @dev Returns the value of tokens in existence.
 26 |     |      */
 27 |     |     function totalSupply() external view returns (uint256);
 28 |     | 
 29 |     |     /**
 30 |     |      * @dev Returns the value of tokens owned by `account`.
 31 |     |      */
 32 |     |     function balanceOf(address account) external view returns (uint256);
 33 |     | 
 34 |     |     /**
 35 |     |      * @dev Moves a `value` amount of tokens from the caller's account to `to`.
 36 |     |      *
 37 |     |      * Returns a boolean value indicating whether the operation succeeded.
 38 |     |      *
 39 |     |      * Emits a {Transfer} event.
 40 |     |      */
 41 |     |     function transfer(address to, uint256 value) external returns (bool);
 42 |     | 
 43 |     |     /**
 44 |     |      * @dev Returns the remaining number of tokens that `spender` will be
 45 |     |      * allowed to spend on behalf of `owner` through {transferFrom}. This is
 46 |     |      * zero by default.
 47 |     |      *
 48 |     |      * This value changes when {approve} or {transferFrom} are called.
 49 |     |      */
 50 |     |     function allowance(address owner, address spender) external view returns (uint256);
 51 |     | 
 52 |     |     /**
 53 |     |      * @dev Sets a `value` amount of tokens as the allowance of `spender` over the
 54 |     |      * caller's tokens.
 55 |     |      *
 56 |     |      * Returns a boolean value indicating whether the operation succeeded.
 57 |     |      *
 58 |     |      * IMPORTANT: Beware that changing an allowance with this method brings the risk
 59 |     |      * that someone may use both the old and the new allowance by unfortunate
 60 |     |      * transaction ordering. One possible solution to mitigate this race
 61 |     |      * condition is to first reduce the spender's allowance to 0 and set the
 62 |     |      * desired value afterwards:
 63 |     |      * https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/issues/20#issuecomment-263524729
 64 |     |      *
 65 |     |      * Emits an {Approval} event.
 66 |     |      */
 67 |     |     function approve(address spender, uint256 value) external returns (bool);
 68 |     |

 73 |     |      *

/home/redkidd/SoloTime/HedgeyFund/valari/valari-contracts/lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/IERC20Permit.sol
  1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
  2 |     | // OpenZeppelin Contracts (last updated v5.0.0) (token/ERC20/extensions/IERC20Permit.sol)
  3 |     | 
  4 |     | pragma solidity ^0.8.20;
  5 |     | 
  6 |     | /**
  7 |     |  * @dev Interface of the ERC20 Permit extension allowing approvals to be made via signatures, as defined in
  8 |     |  * https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612[EIP-2612].
  9 |     |  *
 10 |     |  * Adds the {permit} method, which can be used to change an account's ERC20 allowance (see {IERC20-allowance}) by
 11 |     |  * presenting a message signed by the account. By not relying on {IERC20-approve}, the token holder account doesn't
 12 |     |  * need to send a transaction, and thus is not required to hold Ether at all.
 13 |     |  *
 14 |     |  * ==== Security Considerations
 15 |     |  *
 16 |     |  * There are two important considerations concerning the use of `permit`. The first is that a valid permit signature
 17 |     |  * expresses an allowance, and it should not be assumed to convey additional meaning. In particular, it should not be
 18 |     |  * considered as an intention to spend the allowance in any specific way. The second is that because permits have
 19 |     |  * built-in replay protection and can be submitted by anyone, they can be frontrun. A protocol that uses permits should
 20 |     |  * take this into consideration and allow a `permit` call to fail. Combining these two aspects, a pattern that may be
 21 |     |  * generally recommended is:
 22 |     |  *
 23 |     |  * ```solidity
 24 |     |  * function doThingWithPermit(..., uint256 value, uint256 deadline, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s) public {
 25 |     |  *     try token.permit(msg.sender, address(this), value, deadline, v, r, s) {} catch {}
 26 |     |  *     doThing(..., value);
 27 |     |  * }
 28 |     |  *
 29 |     |  * function doThing(..., uint256 value) public {
 30 |     |  *     token.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), value);
 31 |     |  *     ...
 32 |     |  * }
 33 |     |  * ```
 34 |     |  *
 35 |     |  * Observe that: 1) `msg.sender` is used as the owner, leaving no ambiguity as to the signer intent, and 2) the use of
 36 |     |  * `try/catch` allows the permit to fail and makes the code tolerant to frontrunning. (See also
 37 |     |  * {SafeERC20-safeTransferFrom}).
 38 |     |  *
 39 |     |  * Additionally, note that smart contract wallets (such as Argent or Safe) are not able to produce permit signatures, so
 40 |     |  * contracts should have entry points that don't rely on permit.
 41 |     |  */
 42 |     | interface IERC20Permit {
 43 |     |     /**
 44 |     |      * @dev Sets `value` as the allowance of `spender` over ``owner``'s tokens,
 45 |     |      * given ``owner``'s signed approval.
 46 |     |      *
 47 |     |      * IMPORTANT: The same issues {IERC20-approve} has related to transaction
 48 |     |      * ordering also apply here.
 49 |     |      *
 50 |     |      * Emits an {Approval} event.
 51 |     |      *
 52 |     |      * Requirements:
 53 |     |      *
 54 |     |      * - `spender` cannot be the zero address.
 55 |     |      * - `deadline` must be a timestamp in the future.
 56 |     |      * - `v`, `r` and `s` must be a valid `secp256k1` signature from `owner`
 57 |     |      * over the EIP712-formatted function arguments.
 58 |     |      * - the signature must use ``owner``'s current nonce (see {nonces}).
 59 |     |      *
 60 |     |      * For more information on the signature format, see the
 61 |     |      * https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612#specification[relevant EIP
 62 |     |      * section].
 63 |     |      *
 64 |     |      * CAUTION: See Security Considerations above.
 65 |     |      */
 66 |     |     function permit(
 67 |     |         address owner,

  37 |     |      * taken to not create reentrancy vulnerabilities. Consider using
  38 |     |      * {ReentrancyGuard} or the
