  9 |     |  * Inheriting from `ReentrancyGuard` will make the {nonReentrant} modifier
 10 |     |  * available, which can be applied to functions to make sure there are no nested
 11 |     |  * (reentrant) calls to them.
 12 |     |  *
 13 |     |  * Note that because there is a single `nonReentrant` guard, functions marked as
 14 |     |  * `nonReentrant` may not call one another. This can be worked around by making
 15 |     |  * those functions `private`, and then adding `external` `nonReentrant` entry
 16 |     |  * points to them.
 17 |     |  *
 18 |     |  * TIP: If you would like to learn more about reentrancy and alternative ways
 19 |     |  * to protect against it, check out our blog post
 20 |     |  * https://blog.openzeppelin.com/reentrancy-after-istanbul/[Reentrancy After Istanbul].
 21 |     |  */
 22 |     | abstract contract ReentrancyGuard {
 23 |     |     // Booleans are more expensive than uint256 or any type that takes up a full
 24 |     |     // word because each write operation emits an extra SLOAD to first read the
 25 |     |     // slot's contents, replace the bits taken up by the boolean, and then write
 26 |     |     // back. This is the compiler's defense against contract upgrades and
 27 |     |     // pointer aliasing, and it cannot be disabled.
 28 |     | 
 29 |     |     // The values being non-zero value makes deployment a bit more expensive,
 30 |     |     // but in exchange the refund on every call to nonReentrant will be lower in
 31 |     |     // amount. Since refunds are capped to a percentage of the total
 32 |     |     // transaction's gas, it is best to keep them low in cases like this one, to
 33 |     |     // increase the likelihood of the full refund coming into effect.
 34 | *   |     uint256 private constant NOT_ENTERED = 1;
 35 |     |     uint256 private constant ENTERED = 2;
 36 |     | 
 37 |     |     uint256 private _status;
 38 |     | 
 39 |     |     /**
 40 |     |      * @dev Unauthorized reentrant call.
 41 |     |      */
 42 |     |     error ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall();
 43 |     | 
 44 |     |     constructor() {
 45 |     |         _status = NOT_ENTERED;
 46 |     |     }
 47 |     | 
 48 |     |     /**
 49 |     |      * @dev Prevents a contract from calling itself, directly or indirectly.
 50 |     |      * Calling a `nonReentrant` function from another `nonReentrant`
 51 |     |      * function is not supported. It is possible to prevent this from happening
 52 |     |      * by making the `nonReentrant` function external, and making it call a
 53 |     |      * `private` function that does the actual work.
 54 |     |      */
 55 | *   |     modifier nonReentrant() {
 56 |     |         _nonReentrantBefore();
 57 |     |         _;
 58 |     |         _nonReentrantAfter();
 59 |     |     }
 60 |     | 
 61 | *   |     function _nonReentrantBefore() private {
 62 |     |         // On the first call to nonReentrant, _status will be NOT_ENTERED
 63 | *   |         if (_status == ENTERED) {
 64 |     |             revert ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall();
 65 |     |         }
 66 |     | 
 67 |     |         // Any calls to nonReentrant after this point will fail
 68 |     |         _status = ENTERED;
 69 |     |     }
 70 |     | 
 71 |     |     function _nonReentrantAfter() private {
 72 |     |         // By storing the original value once again, a refund is triggered (see
 73 |     |         // https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2200)
 74 |     |         _status = NOT_ENTERED;
 75 |     |     }
 76 |     | 
 77 |     |     /**
 78 |     |      * @dev Returns true if the reentrancy guard is currently set to "entered", which indicates there is a
 79 |     |      * `nonReentrant` function in the call stack.
 80 |     |      */
 81 |     |     function _reentrancyGuardEntered() internal view returns (bool) {
 82 |     |         return _status == ENTERED;
 83 |     |     }
 84 |     | }
 85 |     |

    7 |     | /**
    8 |     |  * @dev Wrappers over Solidity's uintXX/intXX casting operators with added overflow
    9 |     |  * checks.
   10 |     |  *
   11 |     |  * Downcasting from uint256/int256 in Solidity does not revert on overflow. This can
   12 |     |  * easily result in undesired exploitation or bugs, since developers usually
   13 |     |  * assume that overflows raise errors. `SafeCast` restores this intuition by
   14 |     |  * reverting the transaction when such an operation overflows.

   16 |     |  * Using this library instead of the unchecked operations eliminates an entire
   17 |     |  * class of bugs, so it's recommended to use it always.

/home/redkidd/SoloTime/HedgeyFund/valari/valari-contracts/lib/permit2/src/libraries/SignatureVerification.sol
  1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
  2 |     | pragma solidity ^0.8.17;
  3 |     | 
  4 |     | import {IERC1271} from "../interfaces/IERC1271.sol";
  5 |     | 
  6 |     | library SignatureVerification {
  7 |     |     /// @notice Thrown when the passed in signature is not a valid length
  8 |     |     error InvalidSignatureLength();
  9 |     | 
 10 |     |     /// @notice Thrown when the recovered signer is equal to the zero address
 11 |     |     error InvalidSignature();
 12 |     | 
 13 |     |     /// @notice Thrown when the recovered signer does not equal the claimedSigner
 14 |     |     error InvalidSigner();
 15 |     | 
 16 |     |     /// @notice Thrown when the recovered contract signature is incorrect
 17 |     |     error InvalidContractSignature();
 18 |     | 
 19 | *   |     bytes32 constant UPPER_BIT_MASK = (0x7fffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff);
 20 |     | 
 21 |     |     function verify(bytes calldata signature, bytes32 hash, address claimedSigner) internal view {
 22 |     |         bytes32 r;
 23 |     |         bytes32 s;
 24 |     |         uint8 v;
 25 |     | 
 26 |     |         if (claimedSigner.code.length == 0) {
 27 |     |             if (signature.length == 65) {
 28 |     |                 (r, s) = abi.decode(signature, (bytes32, bytes32));
 29 |     |                 v = uint8(signature[64]);
 30 |     |             } else if (signature.length == 64) {
 31 |     |                 // EIP-2098
 32 |     |                 bytes32 vs;
 33 |     |                 (r, vs) = abi.decode(signature, (bytes32, bytes32));
 34 |     |                 s = vs & UPPER_BIT_MASK;
 35 |     |                 v = uint8(uint256(vs >> 255)) + 27;
 36 |     |             } else {
 37 |     |                 revert InvalidSignatureLength();
 38 |     |             }
 39 |     |             address signer = ecrecover(hash, v, r, s);
 40 |     |             if (signer == address(0)) revert InvalidSignature();
 41 |     |             if (signer != claimedSigner) revert InvalidSigner();
 42 |     |         } else {
 43 |     |             bytes4 magicValue = IERC1271(claimedSigner).isValidSignature(hash, signature);
 44 |     |             if (magicValue != IERC1271.isValidSignature.selector) revert InvalidContractSignature();
 45 |     |         }
 46 |     |     }
 47 |     | }
 48 |     |

 29 |     | 
 30 |     |         emit Transfer(msg.sender, msg.sender, receiver, id, amount);
 31 |     |

 36 |     |         if (msg.sender != sender && !isOperator[sender][msg.sender]) {
 37 |     |             uint256 allowed = allowance[sender][msg.sender][id];
 38 |     |             if (allowed != type(uint256).max) allowance[sender][msg.sender][id] = allowed - amount;
 39 |     |         }

 42 |     | 
 43 |     |         balanceOf[receiver][id] += amount;
 44 |     | 
 45 |     |         emit Transfer(msg.sender, sender, receiver, id, amount);
 46 |     | 
 47 |     |         return true;

 54 |     |

  1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
  2 |     | pragma solidity ^0.8.0;
  3 |     | 
  4 |     | import {IExtsload} from "./interfaces/IExtsload.sol";
  5 |     | 
  6 |     | /// @notice Enables public storage access for efficient state retrieval by external contracts.
  7 |     | /// https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2330#rationale
  8 |     | abstract contract Extsload is IExtsload {
  9 |     |     /// @inheritdoc IExtsload
 10 |     |     function extsload(bytes32 slot) external view returns (bytes32) {
 11 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 12 |     |             mstore(0, sload(slot))
 13 |     |             return(0, 0x20)
 14 |     |         }
 15 |     |     }
 16 |     | 
 17 |     |     /// @inheritdoc IExtsload
 18 |     |     function extsload(bytes32 startSlot, uint256 nSlots) external view returns (bytes32[] memory) {
 19 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 20 |     |             let memptr := mload(0x40)
 21 |     |             let start := memptr
 22 |     |             // A left bit-shift of 5 is equivalent to multiplying by 32 but costs less gas.
 23 |     |             let length := shl(5, nSlots)
 24 |     |             // The abi offset of dynamic array in the returndata is 32.
 25 |     |             mstore(memptr, 0x20)
 26 |     |             // Store the length of the array returned
 27 |     |             mstore(add(memptr, 0x20), nSlots)
 28 |     |             // update memptr to the first location to hold a result
 29 |     |             memptr := add(memptr, 0x40)
 30 |     |             let end := add(memptr, length)
 31 |     |             for {} 1 {} {
 32 |     |                 mstore(memptr, sload(startSlot))
 33 |     |                 memptr := add(memptr, 0x20)
 34 |     |                 startSlot := add(startSlot, 1)
 35 |     |                 if iszero(lt(memptr, end)) { break }
 36 |     |             }
 37 |     |             return(start, sub(end, start))
 38 |     |         }
 39 |     |     }
 40 |     | 
 41 |     |     /// @inheritdoc IExtsload
 42 |     |     function extsload(bytes32[] calldata slots) external view returns (bytes32[] memory) {
 43 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 44 |     |             let memptr := mload(0x40)
 45 |     |             let start := memptr
 46 |     |             // for abi encoding the response - the array will be found at 0x20
 47 |     |             mstore(memptr, 0x20)
 48 |     |             // next we store the length of the return array
 49 |     |             mstore(add(memptr, 0x20), slots.length)
 50 |     |             // update memptr to the first location to hold an array entry
 51 |     |             memptr := add(memptr, 0x40)
 52 |     |             // A left bit-shift of 5 is equivalent to multiplying by 32 but costs less gas.
 53 |     |             let end := add(memptr, shl(5, slots.length))
 54 |     |             let calldataptr := slots.offset
 55 |     |             for {} 1 {} {
 56 |     |                 mstore(memptr, sload(calldataload(calldataptr)))
 57 |     |                 memptr := add(memptr, 0x20)
 58 |     |                 calldataptr := add(calldataptr, 0x20)
 59 |     |                 if iszero(lt(memptr, end)) { break }
 60 |     |             }
 61 |     |             return(start, sub(end, start))
 62 |     |         }
 63 |     |     }
 64 |     | }

 14 |     | /// @notice Contract handling the setting and accrual of protocol fees
 15 |     | abstract contract ProtocolFees is IProtocolFees, Owned {
 16 |     |     using ProtocolFeeLibrary for uint24;
 17 |     |     using Pool for Pool.State;
 18 |     |     using CustomRevert for bytes4;
 19 |     | 
 20 |     |     /// @inheritdoc IProtocolFees
 21 |     |     mapping(Currency currency => uint256 amount) public protocolFeesAccrued;
 22 |     | 
 23 |     |     /// @inheritdoc IProtocolFees
 24 |     |     address public protocolFeeController;
 25 |     | 
 26 |     |     constructor(address initialOwner) Owned(initialOwner) {}
 27 |     | 
 28 |     |     /// @inheritdoc IProtocolFees
 29 |     |     function setProtocolFeeController(address controller) external onlyOwner {
 30 |     |         protocolFeeController = controller;
 31 |     |         emit ProtocolFeeControllerUpdated(controller);
 32 |     |     }
 33 |     | 
 34 |     |     /// @inheritdoc IProtocolFees
 35 |     |     function setProtocolFee(PoolKey memory key, uint24 newProtocolFee) external {
 36 |     |         if (msg.sender != protocolFeeController) InvalidCaller.selector.revertWith();
 37 |     |         if (!newProtocolFee.isValidProtocolFee()) ProtocolFeeTooLarge.selector.revertWith(newProtocolFee);
 38 |     |         PoolId id = key.toId();
 39 |     |         _getPool(id).setProtocolFee(newProtocolFee);
 40 |     |         emit ProtocolFeeUpdated(id, newProtocolFee);
 41 |     |     }
 42 |     | 
 43 |     |     /// @inheritdoc IProtocolFees
 44 |     |     function collectProtocolFees(address recipient, Currency currency, uint256 amount)
 45 |     |         external
 46 |     |         returns (uint256 amountCollected)
 47 |     |     {
 48 |     |         if (msg.sender != protocolFeeController) InvalidCaller.selector.revertWith();
 49 |     |         if (!currency.isAddressZero() && CurrencyReserves.getSyncedCurrency() == currency) {
 50 |     |             // prevent transfer between the sync and settle balanceOfs (native settle uses msg.value)
 51 |     |             ProtocolFeeCurrencySynced.selector.revertWith();
 52 |     |         }
 53 |     | 
 54 |     |         amountCollected = (amount == 0) ? protocolFeesAccrued[currency] : amount;
 55 |     |         protocolFeesAccrued[currency] -= amountCollected;
 56 |     |         currency.transfer(recipient, amountCollected);
 57 |     |     }

   1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
   2 |     | pragma solidity ^0.8.0;
   3 |     | 
   4 |     | import {PoolKey} from "../types/PoolKey.sol";
   5 |     | import {BalanceDelta} from "../types/BalanceDelta.sol";
   6 |     | import {ModifyLiquidityParams, SwapParams} from "../types/PoolOperation.sol";
   7 |     | import {BeforeSwapDelta} from "../types/BeforeSwapDelta.sol";
   8 |     | 
   9 |     | /// @notice V4 decides whether to invoke specific hooks by inspecting the least significant bits
  10 |     | /// of the address that the hooks contract is deployed to.
  11 |     | /// For example, a hooks contract deployed to address: 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000002400
  12 |     | /// has the lowest bits '10 0100 0000 0000' which would cause the 'before initialize' and 'after add liquidity' hooks to be used.
  13 |     | /// See the Hooks library for the full spec.
  14 |     | /// @dev Should only be callable by the v4 PoolManager.
  15 |     | interface IHooks {
  16 |     |     /// @notice The hook called before the state of a pool is initialized
  17 |     |     /// @param sender The initial msg.sender for the initialize call
  18 |     |     /// @param key The key for the pool being initialized
  19 |     |     /// @param sqrtPriceX96 The sqrt(price) of the pool as a Q64.96
  20 |     |     /// @return bytes4 The function selector for the hook
  21 |     |     function beforeInitialize(address sender, PoolKey calldata key, uint160 sqrtPriceX96) external returns (bytes4);
  22 |     | 
  23 |     |     /// @notice The hook called after the state of a pool is initialized
  24 |     |     /// @param sender The initial msg.sender for the initialize call
  25 |     |     /// @param key The key for the pool being initialized
  26 |     |     /// @param sqrtPriceX96 The sqrt(price) of the pool as a Q64.96
  27 |     |     /// @param tick The current tick after the state of a pool is initialized
  28 |     |     /// @return bytes4 The function selector for the hook
  29 |     |     function afterInitialize(address sender, PoolKey calldata key, uint160 sqrtPriceX96, int24 tick)
  30 |     |         external
  31 |     |         returns (bytes4);
  32 |     |

  1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
  2 |     | pragma solidity ^0.8.0;
  3 |     | 
  4 |     | /// @title BitMath
  5 |     | /// @dev This library provides functionality for computing bit properties of an unsigned integer
  6 |     | /// @author Solady (https://github.com/Vectorized/solady/blob/8200a70e8dc2a77ecb074fc2e99a2a0d36547522/src/utils/LibBit.sol)
  7 |     | library BitMath {
  8 |     |     /// @notice Returns the index of the most significant bit of the number,
  9 |     |     ///     where the least significant bit is at index 0 and the most significant bit is at index 255
 10 |     |     /// @param x the value for which to compute the most significant bit, must be greater than 0
 11 |     |     /// @return r the index of the most significant bit
 12 | *   |     function mostSignificantBit(uint256 x) internal pure returns (uint8 r) {
 13 | *   |         require(x > 0);
 14 |     | 
 15 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 16 |     |             r := shl(7, lt(0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff, x))
 17 |     |             r := or(r, shl(6, lt(0xffffffffffffffff, shr(r, x))))
 18 |     |             r := or(r, shl(5, lt(0xffffffff, shr(r, x))))
 19 |     |             r := or(r, shl(4, lt(0xffff, shr(r, x))))
 20 |     |             r := or(r, shl(3, lt(0xff, shr(r, x))))
 21 |     |             // forgefmt: disable-next-item
 22 |     |             r := or(r, byte(and(0x1f, shr(shr(r, x), 0x8421084210842108cc6318c6db6d54be)),
 23 |     |                 0x0706060506020500060203020504000106050205030304010505030400000000))
 24 |     |         }
 25 |     |     }
 26 |     | 
 27 |     |     /// @notice Returns the index of the least significant bit of the number,
 28 |     |     ///     where the least significant bit is at index 0 and the most significant bit is at index 255
 29 |     |     /// @param x the value for which to compute the least significant bit, must be greater than 0
 30 |     |     /// @return r the index of the least significant bit
 31 |     |     function leastSignificantBit(uint256 x) internal pure returns (uint8 r) {
 32 |     |         require(x > 0);
 33 |     | 
 34 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 35 |     |             // Isolate the least significant bit.
 36 |     |             x := and(x, sub(0, x))
 37 |     |             // For the upper 3 bits of the result, use a De Bruijn-like lookup.
 38 |     |             // Credit to adhusson: https://blog.adhusson.com/cheap-find-first-set-evm/
 39 |     |             // forgefmt: disable-next-item
 40 |     |             r := shl(5, shr(252, shl(shl(2, shr(250, mul(x,
 41 |     |                 0xb6db6db6ddddddddd34d34d349249249210842108c6318c639ce739cffffffff))),
 42 |     |                 0x8040405543005266443200005020610674053026020000107506200176117077)))
 43 |     |             // For the lower 5 bits of the result, use a De Bruijn lookup.
 44 |     |             // forgefmt: disable-next-item
 45 |     |             r := or(r, byte(and(div(0xd76453e0, shr(r, x)), 0x1f),
 46 |     |                 0x001f0d1e100c1d070f090b19131c1706010e11080a1a141802121b1503160405))
 47 |     |         }
 48 |     |     }
 49 |     | }

  7 |     | /// @dev this library implements the equivalent of a mapping, as transient storage can only be accessed in assembly
  8 |     | library CurrencyDelta {
  9 |     |     /// @notice calculates which storage slot a delta should be stored in for a given account and currency
 10 |     |     function _computeSlot(address target, Currency currency) internal pure returns (bytes32 hashSlot) {
 11 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 12 |     |             mstore(0, and(target, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff))
 13 |     |             mstore(32, and(currency, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff))
 14 |     |             hashSlot := keccak256(0, 64)
 15 |     |         }
 16 |     |     }
 17 |     |

 19 |     |         bytes32 hashSlot = _computeSlot(target, currency);
 20 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 21 |     |             delta := tload(hashSlot)
 22 |     |         }
 23 |     |     }
 24 |     | 
 25 |     |     /// @notice applies a new currency delta for a given account and currency
 26 |     |     /// @return previous The prior value
 27 |     |     /// @return next The modified result
 28 |     |     function applyDelta(Currency currency, address target, int128 delta)
 29 |     |         internal
 30 |     |         returns (int256 previous, int256 next)
 31 |     |     {

 33 |     | 
 34 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 35 |     |             previous := tload(hashSlot)
 36 |     |         }
 37 | *   |         next = previous + delta;
 38 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 39 |     |             tstore(hashSlot, next)

   1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
   2 |     | pragma solidity ^0.8.0;
   3 |     | 
   4 |     | /// @title Library for reverting with custom errors efficiently
   5 |     | /// @notice Contains functions for reverting with custom errors with different argument types efficiently
   6 |     | /// @dev To use this library, declare `using CustomRevert for bytes4;` and replace `revert CustomError()` with
   7 |     | /// `CustomError.selector.revertWith()`
   8 |     | /// @dev The functions may tamper with the free memory pointer but it is fine since the call context is exited immediately
   9 |     | library CustomRevert {
  10 |     |     /// @dev ERC-7751 error for wrapping bubbled up reverts
  11 |     |     error WrappedError(address target, bytes4 selector, bytes reason, bytes details);
  12 |     | 
  13 |     |     /// @dev Reverts with the selector of a custom error in the scratch space
  14 |     |     function revertWith(bytes4 selector) internal pure {
  15 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
  16 |     |             mstore(0, selector)
  17 |     |             revert(0, 0x04)
  18 |     |         }
  19 |     |     }
  20 |     | 
  21 |     |     /// @dev Reverts with a custom error with an address argument in the scratch space
  22 |     |     function revertWith(bytes4 selector, address addr) internal pure {
  23 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
  24 |     |             mstore(0, selector)
  25 |     |             mstore(0x04, and(addr, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff))
  26 |     |             revert(0, 0x24)
  27 |     |         }
  28 |     |     }
  29 |     | 
  30 |     |     /// @dev Reverts with a custom error with an int24 argument in the scratch space
  31 |     |     function revertWith(bytes4 selector, int24 value) internal pure {
  32 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
  33 |     |             mstore(0, selector)
  34 |     |             mstore(0x04, signextend(2, value))
  35 |     |             revert(0, 0x24)
  36 |     |         }
  37 |     |     }
  38 |     | 
  39 |     |     /// @dev Reverts with a custom error with a uint160 argument in the scratch space
  40 |     |     function revertWith(bytes4 selector, uint160 value) internal pure {
  41 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
  42 |     |             mstore(0, selector)
  43 |     |             mstore(0x04, and(value, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff))
  44 |     |             revert(0, 0x24)
  45 |     |         }
  46 |     |     }
  47 |     | 
  48 |     |     /// @dev Reverts with a custom error with two int24 arguments
  49 |     |     function revertWith(bytes4 selector, int24 value1, int24 value2) internal pure {
  50 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
  51 |     |             let fmp := mload(0x40)
  52 |     |             mstore(fmp, selector)
  53 |     |             mstore(add(fmp, 0x04), signextend(2, value1))
  54 |     |             mstore(add(fmp, 0x24), signextend(2, value2))
  55 |     |             revert(fmp, 0x44)
  56 |     |         }
  57 |     |     }
  58 |     | 
  59 |     |     /// @dev Reverts with a custom error with two uint160 arguments
  60 |     |     function revertWith(bytes4 selector, uint160 value1, uint160 value2) internal pure {
  61 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
  62 |     |             let fmp := mload(0x40)
  63 |     |             mstore(fmp, selector)
  64 |     |             mstore(add(fmp, 0x04), and(value1, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff))
  65 |     |             mstore(add(fmp, 0x24), and(value2, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff))
  66 |     |             revert(fmp, 0x44)
  67 |     |         }
  68 |     |     }
  69 |     | 
  70 |     |     /// @dev Reverts with a custom error with two address arguments
  71 |     |     function revertWith(bytes4 selector, address value1, address value2) internal pure {
  72 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
  73 |     |             let fmp := mload(0x40)
  74 |     |             mstore(fmp, selector)
  75 |     |             mstore(add(fmp, 0x04), and(value1, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff))
  76 |     |             mstore(add(fmp, 0x24), and(value2, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff))
  77 |     |             revert(fmp, 0x44)
  78 |     |         }
  79 |     |     }
  80 |     | 
  81 |     |     /// @notice bubble up the revert message returned by a call and revert with a wrapped ERC-7751 error
  82 |     |     /// @dev this method can be vulnerable to revert data bombs
  83 |     |     function bubbleUpAndRevertWith(
  84 |     |         address revertingContract,
  85 |     |         bytes4 revertingFunctionSelector,
  86 |     |         bytes4 additionalContext
  87 |     |     ) internal pure {
  88 |     |         bytes4 wrappedErrorSelector = WrappedError.selector;
  89 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
  90 |     |             // Ensure the size of the revert data is a multiple of 32 bytes
  91 |     |             let encodedDataSize := mul(div(add(returndatasize(), 31), 32), 32)
  92 |     | 
  93 |     |             let fmp := mload(0x40)
  94 |     | 
  95 |     |             // Encode wrapped error selector, address, function selector, offset, additional context, size, revert reason
  96 |     |             mstore(fmp, wrappedErrorSelector)
  97 |     |             mstore(add(fmp, 0x04), and(revertingContract, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff))
  98 |     |             mstore(
  99 |     |                 add(fmp, 0x24),
 100 |     |                 and(revertingFunctionSelector, 0xffffffff00000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000)
 101 |     |             )
 102 |     |             // offset revert reason
 103 |     |             mstore(add(fmp, 0x44), 0x80)
 104 |     |             // offset additional context
 105 |     |             mstore(add(fmp, 0x64), add(0xa0, encodedDataSize))
 106 |     |             // size revert reason
 107 |     |             mstore(add(fmp, 0x84), returndatasize())
 108 |     |             // revert reason
 109 |     |             returndatacopy(add(fmp, 0xa4), 0, returndatasize())
 110 |     |             // size additional context
 111 |     |             mstore(add(fmp, add(0xa4, encodedDataSize)), 0x04)
 112 |     |             // additional context
 113 |     |             mstore(
 114 |     |                 add(fmp, add(0xc4, encodedDataSize)),
 115 |     |                 and(additionalContext, 0xffffffff00000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000)
 116 |     |             )
 117 |     |             revert(fmp, add(0xe4, encodedDataSize))
 118 |     |         }
 119 |     |     }

/home/redkidd/SoloTime/HedgeyFund/valari/valari-contracts/lib/v4-core/src/libraries/FullMath.sol
   1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
   2 |     | pragma solidity ^0.8.0;
   3 |     | 
   4 |     | /// @title Contains 512-bit math functions
   5 |     | /// @notice Facilitates multiplication and division that can have overflow of an intermediate value without any loss of precision
   6 |     | /// @dev Handles "phantom overflow" i.e., allows multiplication and division where an intermediate value overflows 256 bits
   7 |     | library FullMath {
   8 |     |     /// @notice Calculates floor(a×b÷denominator) with full precision. Throws if result overflows a uint256 or denominator == 0
   9 |     |     /// @param a The multiplicand
  10 |     |     /// @param b The multiplier
  11 |     |     /// @param denominator The divisor
  12 |     |     /// @return result The 256-bit result
  13 |     |     /// @dev Credit to Remco Bloemen under MIT license https://xn--2-umb.com/21/muldiv
  14 | *   |     function mulDiv(uint256 a, uint256 b, uint256 denominator) internal pure returns (uint256 result) {
  15 |     |         unchecked {
  16 |     |             // 512-bit multiply [prod1 prod0] = a * b
  17 |     |             // Compute the product mod 2**256 and mod 2**256 - 1
  18 |     |             // then use the Chinese Remainder Theorem to reconstruct
  19 |     |             // the 512 bit result. The result is stored in two 256
  20 |     |             // variables such that product = prod1 * 2**256 + prod0
  21 |     |             uint256 prod0 = a * b; // Least significant 256 bits of the product
  22 |     |             uint256 prod1; // Most significant 256 bits of the product
  23 | *   |             assembly ("memory-safe") {
  24 |     |                 let mm := mulmod(a, b, not(0))
  25 |     |                 prod1 := sub(sub(mm, prod0), lt(mm, prod0))
  26 |     |             }
  27 |     | 
  28 |     |             // Make sure the result is less than 2**256.
  29 |     |             // Also prevents denominator == 0
  30 | *   |             require(denominator > prod1);
  31 |     | 
  32 |     |             // Handle non-overflow cases, 256 by 256 division
  33 | *   |             if (prod1 == 0) {
  34 | *   |                 assembly ("memory-safe") {
  35 |     |                     result := div(prod0, denominator)
  36 |     |                 }
  37 | *   |                 return result;
  38 |     |             }
  39 |     | 
  40 |     |             ///////////////////////////////////////////////
  41 |     |             // 512 by 256 division.
  42 |     |             ///////////////////////////////////////////////
  43 |     | 
  44 |     |             // Make division exact by subtracting the remainder from [prod1 prod0]
  45 |     |             // Compute remainder using mulmod
  46 |     |             uint256 remainder;
  47 | *   |             assembly ("memory-safe") {
  48 |     |                 remainder := mulmod(a, b, denominator)
  49 |     |             }
  50 |     |             // Subtract 256 bit number from 512 bit number
  51 | *   |             assembly ("memory-safe") {
  52 |     |                 prod1 := sub(prod1, gt(remainder, prod0))
  53 |     |                 prod0 := sub(prod0, remainder)
  54 |     |             }
  55 |     | 
  56 |     |             // Factor powers of two out of denominator
  57 |     |             // Compute largest power of two divisor of denominator.
  58 |     |             // Always >= 1.
  59 | *   |             uint256 twos = (0 - denominator) & denominator;
  60 |     |             // Divide denominator by power of two
  61 | *   |             assembly ("memory-safe") {
  62 |     |                 denominator := div(denominator, twos)
  63 |     |             }
  64 |     | 
  65 |     |             // Divide [prod1 prod0] by the factors of two
  66 | *   |             assembly ("memory-safe") {
  67 |     |                 prod0 := div(prod0, twos)
  68 |     |             }
  69 |     |             // Shift in bits from prod1 into prod0. For this we need
  70 |     |             // to flip `twos` such that it is 2**256 / twos.
  71 |     |             // If twos is zero, then it becomes one
  72 | *   |             assembly ("memory-safe") {
  73 |     |                 twos := add(div(sub(0, twos), twos), 1)
  74 |     |             }
  75 | *   |             prod0 |= prod1 * twos;
  76 |     | 
  77 |     |             // Invert denominator mod 2**256
  78 |     |             // Now that denominator is an odd number, it has an inverse
  79 |     |             // modulo 2**256 such that denominator * inv = 1 mod 2**256.
  80 |     |             // Compute the inverse by starting with a seed that is correct
  81 |     |             // correct for four bits. That is, denominator * inv = 1 mod 2**4
  82 | *   |             uint256 inv = (3 * denominator) ^ 2;
  83 |     |             // Now use Newton-Raphson iteration to improve the precision.
  84 |     |             // Thanks to Hensel's lifting lemma, this also works in modular
  85 |     |             // arithmetic, doubling the correct bits in each step.
  86 |     |             inv *= 2 - denominator * inv; // inverse mod 2**8
  87 |     |             inv *= 2 - denominator * inv; // inverse mod 2**16
  88 |     |             inv *= 2 - denominator * inv; // inverse mod 2**32
  89 |     |             inv *= 2 - denominator * inv; // inverse mod 2**64
  90 |     |             inv *= 2 - denominator * inv; // inverse mod 2**128
  91 |     |             inv *= 2 - denominator * inv; // inverse mod 2**256
  92 |     | 
  93 |     |             // Because the division is now exact we can divide by multiplying
  94 |     |             // with the modular inverse of denominator. This will give us the
  95 |     |             // correct result modulo 2**256. Since the preconditions guarantee
  96 |     |             // that the outcome is less than 2**256, this is the final result.
  97 |     |             // We don't need to compute the high bits of the result and prod1
  98 |     |             // is no longer required.
  99 |     |             result = prod0 * inv;
 100 |     |             return result;
 101 |     |         }
 102 |     |     }
 103 |     | 
 104 |     |     /// @notice Calculates ceil(a×b÷denominator) with full precision. Throws if result overflows a uint256 or denominator == 0
 105 |     |     /// @param a The multiplicand
 106 |     |     /// @param b The multiplier
 107 |     |     /// @param denominator The divisor
 108 |     |     /// @return result The 256-bit result
 109 | *   |     function mulDivRoundingUp(uint256 a, uint256 b, uint256 denominator) internal pure returns (uint256 result) {
 110 |     |         unchecked {
 111 | *   |             result = mulDiv(a, b, denominator);
 112 | *   |             if (mulmod(a, b, denominator) != 0) {
 113 | *   |                 require(++result > 0);
 114 |     |             }
 115 |     |         }
 116 |     |     }

 129 |     |     /// @notice performs a hook call using the given calldata on the given hook that doesn't return a delta
 130 |     |     /// @return result The complete data returned by the hook
 131 |     |     function callHook(IHooks self, bytes memory data) internal returns (bytes memory result) {
 132 |     |         bool success;
 133 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 134 |     |             success := call(gas(), self, 0, add(data, 0x20), mload(data), 0, 0)
 135 |     |         }
 136 |     |         // Revert with FailedHookCall, containing any error message to bubble up
 137 |     |         if (!success) CustomRevert.bubbleUpAndRevertWith(address(self), bytes4(data), HookCallFailed.selector);
 138 |     | 
 139 |     |         // The call was successful, fetch the returned data
 140 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 141 |     |             // allocate result byte array from the free memory pointer
 142 |     |             result := mload(0x40)
 143 |     |             // store new free memory pointer at the end of the array padded to 32 bytes
 144 |     |             mstore(0x40, add(result, and(add(returndatasize(), 0x3f), not(0x1f))))
 145 |     |             // store length in memory
 146 |     |             mstore(result, returndatasize())
 147 |     |             // copy return data to result
 148 |     |             returndatacopy(add(result, 0x20), 0, returndatasize())
 149 |     |         }
 150 |     | 
 151 |     |         // Length must be at least 32 to contain the selector. Check expected selector and returned selector match.
 152 |     |         if (result.length < 32 || result.parseSelector() != data.parseSelector()) {
 153 |     |             InvalidHookResponse.selector.revertWith();
 154 |     |         }
 155 |     |     }

 168 |     |     }

 560 |     |     /// @notice Derives max liquidity per tick from given tick spacing
 561 |     |     /// @dev Executed when adding liquidity
 562 |     |     /// @param tickSpacing The amount of required tick separation, realized in multiples of `tickSpacing`
 563 |     |     ///     e.g., a tickSpacing of 3 requires ticks to be initialized every 3rd tick i.e., ..., -6, -3, 0, 3, 6, ...
 564 |     |     /// @return result The max liquidity per tick
 565 |     |     function tickSpacingToMaxLiquidityPerTick(int24 tickSpacing) internal pure returns (uint128 result) {
 566 |     |         // Equivalent to:
 567 |     |         // int24 minTick = (TickMath.MIN_TICK / tickSpacing);
 568 |     |         // if (TickMath.MIN_TICK  % tickSpacing != 0) minTick--;
 569 |     |         // int24 maxTick = (TickMath.MAX_TICK / tickSpacing);
 570 |     |         // uint24 numTicks = maxTick - minTick + 1;
 571 |     |         // return type(uint128).max / numTicks;
 572 |     |         int24 MAX_TICK = TickMath.MAX_TICK;
 573 |     |         int24 MIN_TICK = TickMath.MIN_TICK;
 574 |     |         // tick spacing will never be 0 since TickMath.MIN_TICK_SPACING is 1
 575 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 576 |     |             tickSpacing := signextend(2, tickSpacing)
 577 |     |             let minTick := sub(sdiv(MIN_TICK, tickSpacing), slt(smod(MIN_TICK, tickSpacing), 0))
 578 |     |             let maxTick := sdiv(MAX_TICK, tickSpacing)
 579 |     |             let numTicks := add(sub(maxTick, minTick), 1)
 580 |     |             result := div(sub(shl(128, 1), 1), numTicks)
 581 |     |         }
 582 |     |     }

  1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
  2 |     | pragma solidity ^0.8.0;
  3 |     | 
  4 |     | /// @notice library of functions related to protocol fees
  5 |     | library ProtocolFeeLibrary {
  6 |     |     /// @notice Max protocol fee is 0.1% (1000 pips)
  7 |     |     /// @dev Increasing these values could lead to overflow in Pool.swap
  8 |     |     uint16 public constant MAX_PROTOCOL_FEE = 1000;
  9 |     | 
 10 |     |     /// @notice Thresholds used for optimized bounds checks on protocol fees
 11 |     |     uint24 internal constant FEE_0_THRESHOLD = 1001;
 12 |     |     uint24 internal constant FEE_1_THRESHOLD = 1001 << 12;
 13 |     | 
 14 |     |     /// @notice the protocol fee is represented in hundredths of a bip
 15 | *   |     uint256 internal constant PIPS_DENOMINATOR = 1_000_000;
 16 |     | 
 17 |     |     function getZeroForOneFee(uint24 self) internal pure returns (uint16) {
 18 | *   |         return uint16(self & 0xfff);
 19 |     |     }
 20 |     | 
 21 |     |     function getOneForZeroFee(uint24 self) internal pure returns (uint16) {
 22 |     |         return uint16(self >> 12);
 23 |     |     }
 24 |     | 
 25 |     |     function isValidProtocolFee(uint24 self) internal pure returns (bool valid) {
 26 |     |         // Equivalent to: getZeroForOneFee(self) <= MAX_PROTOCOL_FEE && getOneForZeroFee(self) <= MAX_PROTOCOL_FEE
 27 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 28 |     |             let isZeroForOneFeeOk := lt(and(self, 0xfff), FEE_0_THRESHOLD)
 29 |     |             let isOneForZeroFeeOk := lt(and(self, 0xfff000), FEE_1_THRESHOLD)
 30 |     |             valid := and(isZeroForOneFeeOk, isOneForZeroFeeOk)
 31 |     |         }
 32 |     |     }
 33 |     | 
 34 |     |     // The protocol fee is taken from the input amount first and then the LP fee is taken from the remaining
 35 |     |     // The swap fee is capped at 100%
 36 |     |     // Equivalent to protocolFee + lpFee(1_000_000 - protocolFee) / 1_000_000 (rounded up)
 37 |     |     /// @dev here `self` is just a single direction's protocol fee, not a packed type of 2 protocol fees
 38 |     |     function calculateSwapFee(uint16 self, uint24 lpFee) internal pure returns (uint24 swapFee) {
 39 |     |         // protocolFee + lpFee - (protocolFee * lpFee / 1_000_000)
 40 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 41 |     |             self := and(self, 0xfff)
 42 |     |             lpFee := and(lpFee, 0xffffff)
 43 |     |             let numerator := mul(self, lpFee)
 44 |     |             swapFee := sub(add(self, lpFee), div(numerator, PIPS_DENOMINATOR))
 45 |     |         }
 46 |     |     }
 47 |     | }

  10 |     | /// @title Functions based on Q64.96 sqrt price and liquidity
  11 |     | /// @notice Contains the math that uses square root of price as a Q64.96 and liquidity to compute deltas
  12 |     | library SqrtPriceMath {
  13 |     |     using SafeCast for uint256;
  14 |     | 
  15 |     |     error InvalidPriceOrLiquidity();

  20 |     |     /// @notice Gets the next sqrt price given a delta of currency0
  21 |     |     /// @dev Always rounds up, because in the exact output case (increasing price) we need to move the price at least
  22 |     |     /// far enough to get the desired output amount, and in the exact input case (decreasing price) we need to move the
  23 |     |     /// price less in order to not send too much output.
  24 |     |     /// The most precise formula for this is liquidity * sqrtPX96 / (liquidity +- amount * sqrtPX96),
  25 |     |     /// if this is impossible because of overflow, we calculate liquidity / (liquidity / sqrtPX96 +- amount).
  26 |     |     /// @param sqrtPX96 The starting price, i.e. before accounting for the currency0 delta
  27 |     |     /// @param liquidity The amount of usable liquidity
  28 |     |     /// @param amount How much of currency0 to add or remove from virtual reserves
  29 |     |     /// @param add Whether to add or remove the amount of currency0
  30 |     |     /// @return The price after adding or removing amount, depending on add
  31 | *   |     function getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp(uint160 sqrtPX96, uint128 liquidity, uint256 amount, bool add)
  32 |     |         internal
  33 |     |         pure
  34 |     |         returns (uint160)
  35 |     |     {
  36 |     |         // we short circuit amount == 0 because the result is otherwise not guaranteed to equal the input price
  37 | *   |         if (amount == 0) return sqrtPX96;
  38 |     |         uint256 numerator1 = uint256(liquidity) << FixedPoint96.RESOLUTION;
  39 |     | 
  40 |     |         if (add) {
  41 |     |             unchecked {
  42 |     |                 uint256 product = amount * sqrtPX96;
  43 | *   |                 if (product / amount == sqrtPX96) {
  44 |     |                     uint256 denominator = numerator1 + product;
  45 | *   |                     if (denominator >= numerator1) {
  46 |     |                         // always fits in 160 bits
  47 | *   |                         return uint160(FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp(numerator1, sqrtPX96, denominator));
  48 |     |                     }
  49 |     |                 }
  50 |     |             }
  51 |     |             // denominator is checked for overflow
  52 |     |             return uint160(UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp(numerator1, (numerator1 / sqrtPX96) + amount));
  53 |     |         } else {
  54 |     |             unchecked {
  55 |     |                 uint256 product = amount * sqrtPX96;
  56 |     |                 // if the product overflows, we know the denominator underflows
  57 |     |                 // in addition, we must check that the denominator does not underflow
  58 |     |                 // equivalent: if (product / amount != sqrtPX96 || numerator1 <= product) revert PriceOverflow();
  59 |     |                 assembly ("memory-safe") {
  60 |     |                     if iszero(
  61 |     |                         and(
  62 |     |                             eq(div(product, amount), and(sqrtPX96, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff)),
  63 |     |                             gt(numerator1, product)
  64 |     |                         )
  65 |     |                     ) {
  66 |     |                         mstore(0, 0xf5c787f1) // selector for PriceOverflow()
  67 |     |                         revert(0x1c, 0x04)
  68 |     |                     }
  69 |     |                 }
  70 |     |                 uint256 denominator = numerator1 - product;
  71 |     |                 return FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp(numerator1, sqrtPX96, denominator).toUint160();
  72 |     |             }
  73 |     |         }
  74 |     |     }

  79 |     |     /// price less in order to not send too much output.
  80 |     |     /// The formula we compute is within <1 wei of the lossless version: sqrtPX96 +- amount / liquidity
  81 |     |     /// @param sqrtPX96 The starting price, i.e., before accounting for the currency1 delta

  87 |     |         internal

  94 |     |             uint256 quotient = (
  95 | *   |                 amount <= type(uint160).max

 101 |     |         } else {
 102 |     |             uint256 quotient = (
 103 |     |                 amount <= type(uint160).max
 104 |     |                     ? UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp(amount << FixedPoint96.RESOLUTION, liquidity)
 105 |     |                     : FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp(amount, FixedPoint96.Q96, liquidity)

 114 |     |             }

 116 |     |             unchecked {

 119 |     |         }

 183 |     |     /// @param sqrtPriceAX96 A sqrt price

 213 |     |     /// @notice Equivalent to: `a >= b ? a - b : b - a`
 214 |     |     function absDiff(uint160 a, uint160 b) internal pure returns (uint256 res) {
 215 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 216 |     |             let diff :=
 217 |     |                 sub(and(a, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff), and(b, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff))
 218 |     |             // mask = 0 if a >= b else -1 (all 1s)
 219 |     |             let mask := sar(255, diff)
 220 |     |             // if a >= b, res = a - b = 0 ^ (a - b)
 221 |     |             // if a < b, res = b - a = ~~(b - a) = ~(-(b - a) - 1) = ~(a - b - 1) = (-1) ^ (a - b - 1)
 222 |     |             // either way, res = mask ^ (a - b + mask)
 223 |     |             res := xor(mask, add(mask, diff))
 224 |     |         }
 225 |     |     }

   7 |     | /// @title Computes the result of a swap within ticks
   8 |     | /// @notice Contains methods for computing the result of a swap within a single tick price range, i.e., a single tick.
   9 |     | library SwapMath {
  10 |     |     /// @notice the swap fee is represented in hundredths of a bip, so the max is 100%
  11 |     |     /// @dev the swap fee is the total fee on a swap, including both LP and Protocol fee
  12 | *   |     uint256 internal constant MAX_SWAP_FEE = 1e6;
  13 |     | 
  14 |     |     /// @notice Computes the sqrt price target for the next swap step
  15 |     |     /// @param zeroForOne The direction of the swap, true for currency0 to currency1, false for currency1 to currency0
  16 |     |     /// @param sqrtPriceNextX96 The Q64.96 sqrt price for the next initialized tick
  17 |     |     /// @param sqrtPriceLimitX96 The Q64.96 sqrt price limit. If zero for one, the price cannot be less than this value
  18 |     |     /// after the swap. If one for zero, the price cannot be greater than this value after the swap
  19 |     |     /// @return sqrtPriceTargetX96 The price target for the next swap step
  20 |     |     function getSqrtPriceTarget(bool zeroForOne, uint160 sqrtPriceNextX96, uint160 sqrtPriceLimitX96)
  21 |     |         internal
  22 |     |         pure
  23 |     |         returns (uint160 sqrtPriceTargetX96)
  24 |     |     {
  25 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
  26 |     |             // a flag to toggle between sqrtPriceNextX96 and sqrtPriceLimitX96
  27 |     |             // when zeroForOne == true, nextOrLimit reduces to sqrtPriceNextX96 >= sqrtPriceLimitX96
  28 |     |             // sqrtPriceTargetX96 = max(sqrtPriceNextX96, sqrtPriceLimitX96)
  29 |     |             // when zeroForOne == false, nextOrLimit reduces to sqrtPriceNextX96 < sqrtPriceLimitX96
  30 |     |             // sqrtPriceTargetX96 = min(sqrtPriceNextX96, sqrtPriceLimitX96)
  31 |     |             sqrtPriceNextX96 := and(sqrtPriceNextX96, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff)
  32 |     |             sqrtPriceLimitX96 := and(sqrtPriceLimitX96, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff)
  33 |     |             let nextOrLimit := xor(lt(sqrtPriceNextX96, sqrtPriceLimitX96), and(zeroForOne, 0x1))
  34 |     |             let symDiff := xor(sqrtPriceNextX96, sqrtPriceLimitX96)
  35 |     |             sqrtPriceTargetX96 := xor(sqrtPriceLimitX96, mul(symDiff, nextOrLimit))
  36 |     |         }
  37 |     |     }
  38 |     | 
  39 |     |     /// @notice Computes the result of swapping some amount in, or amount out, given the parameters of the swap
  40 |     |     /// @dev If the swap's amountSpecified is negative, the combined fee and input amount will never exceed the absolute value of the remaining amount.
  41 |     |     /// @param sqrtPriceCurrentX96 The current sqrt price of the pool
  42 |     |     /// @param sqrtPriceTargetX96 The price that cannot be exceeded, from which the direction of the swap is inferred
  43 |     |     /// @param liquidity The usable liquidity
  44 |     |     /// @param amountRemaining How much input or output amount is remaining to be swapped in/out
  45 |     |     /// @param feePips The fee taken from the input amount, expressed in hundredths of a bip
  46 |     |     /// @return sqrtPriceNextX96 The price after swapping the amount in/out, not to exceed the price target
  47 |     |     /// @return amountIn The amount to be swapped in, of either currency0 or currency1, based on the direction of the swap
  48 |     |     /// @return amountOut The amount to be received, of either currency0 or currency1, based on the direction of the swap
  49 |     |     /// @return feeAmount The amount of input that will be taken as a fee
  50 |     |     /// @dev feePips must be no larger than MAX_SWAP_FEE for this function. We ensure that before setting a fee using LPFeeLibrary.isValid.
  51 |     |     function computeSwapStep(
  52 |     |         uint160 sqrtPriceCurrentX96,
  53 |     |         uint160 sqrtPriceTargetX96,
  54 |     |         uint128 liquidity,
  55 |     |         int256 amountRemaining,
  56 |     |         uint24 feePips
  57 |     |     ) internal pure returns (uint160 sqrtPriceNextX96, uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOut, uint256 feeAmount) {
  58 |     |         unchecked {
  59 |     |             uint256 _feePips = feePips; // upcast once and cache
  60 | *   |             bool zeroForOne = sqrtPriceCurrentX96 >= sqrtPriceTargetX96;
  61 | *   |             bool exactIn = amountRemaining < 0;
  62 |     | 
  63 | *   |             if (exactIn) {
  64 |     |                 uint256 amountRemainingLessFee =
  65 | *   |                     FullMath.mulDiv(uint256(-amountRemaining), MAX_SWAP_FEE - _feePips, MAX_SWAP_FEE);
  66 | *   |                 amountIn = zeroForOne
  67 | *   |                     ? SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta(sqrtPriceTargetX96, sqrtPriceCurrentX96, liquidity, true)
  68 | *   |                     : SqrtPriceMath.getAmount1Delta(sqrtPriceCurrentX96, sqrtPriceTargetX96, liquidity, true);
  69 | *   |                 if (amountRemainingLessFee >= amountIn) {
  70 |     |                     // `amountIn` is capped by the target price
  71 | *   |                     sqrtPriceNextX96 = sqrtPriceTargetX96;
  72 | *   |                     feeAmount = _feePips == MAX_SWAP_FEE
  73 |     |                         ? amountIn // amountIn is always 0 here, as amountRemainingLessFee == 0 and amountRemainingLessFee >= amountIn
  74 | *   |                         : FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp(amountIn, _feePips, MAX_SWAP_FEE - _feePips);
  75 |     |                 } else {
  76 |     |                     // exhaust the remaining amount
  77 | *   |                     amountIn = amountRemainingLessFee;
  78 |     |                     sqrtPriceNextX96 = SqrtPriceMath.getNextSqrtPriceFromInput(
  79 |     |                         sqrtPriceCurrentX96, liquidity, amountRemainingLessFee, zeroForOne
  80 |     |                     );
  81 |     |                     // we didn't reach the target, so take the remainder of the maximum input as fee
  82 |     |                     feeAmount = uint256(-amountRemaining) - amountIn;
  83 |     |                 }
  84 | *   |                 amountOut = zeroForOne
  85 | *   |                     ? SqrtPriceMath.getAmount1Delta(sqrtPriceNextX96, sqrtPriceCurrentX96, liquidity, false)
  86 | *   |                     : SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta(sqrtPriceCurrentX96, sqrtPriceNextX96, liquidity, false);
  87 |     |             } else {
  88 |     |                 amountOut = zeroForOne
  89 |     |                     ? SqrtPriceMath.getAmount1Delta(sqrtPriceTargetX96, sqrtPriceCurrentX96, liquidity, false)
  90 |     |                     : SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta(sqrtPriceCurrentX96, sqrtPriceTargetX96, liquidity, false);
  91 |     |                 if (uint256(amountRemaining) >= amountOut) {
  92 |     |                     // `amountOut` is capped by the target price
  93 |     |                     sqrtPriceNextX96 = sqrtPriceTargetX96;
  94 |     |                 } else {
  95 |     |                     // cap the output amount to not exceed the remaining output amount
  96 |     |                     amountOut = uint256(amountRemaining);
  97 |     |                     sqrtPriceNextX96 =
  98 |     |                         SqrtPriceMath.getNextSqrtPriceFromOutput(sqrtPriceCurrentX96, liquidity, amountOut, zeroForOne);
  99 |     |                 }
 100 |     |                 amountIn = zeroForOne
 101 |     |                     ? SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta(sqrtPriceNextX96, sqrtPriceCurrentX96, liquidity, true)
 102 |     |                     : SqrtPriceMath.getAmount1Delta(sqrtPriceCurrentX96, sqrtPriceNextX96, liquidity, true);
 103 |     |                 // `feePips` cannot be `MAX_SWAP_FEE` for exact out
 104 |     |                 feeAmount = FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp(amountIn, _feePips, MAX_SWAP_FEE - _feePips);
 105 |     |             }
 106 |     |         }
 107 |     |     }
 108 |     | }

   1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
   2 |     | pragma solidity ^0.8.0;
   3 |     | 
   4 |     | import {BitMath} from "./BitMath.sol";
   5 |     | 
   6 |     | /// @title Packed tick initialized state library
   7 |     | /// @notice Stores a packed mapping of tick index to its initialized state
   8 |     | /// @dev The mapping uses int16 for keys since ticks are represented as int24 and there are 256 (2^8) values per word.
   9 |     | library TickBitmap {
  10 |     |     /// @notice Thrown when the tick is not enumerated by the tick spacing
  11 |     |     /// @param tick the invalid tick
  12 |     |     /// @param tickSpacing The tick spacing of the pool
  13 |     |     error TickMisaligned(int24 tick, int24 tickSpacing);
  14 |     | 
  15 |     |     /// @dev round towards negative infinity
  16 |     |     function compress(int24 tick, int24 tickSpacing) internal pure returns (int24 compressed) {
  17 |     |         // compressed = tick / tickSpacing;
  18 |     |         // if (tick < 0 && tick % tickSpacing != 0) compressed--;
  19 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
  20 |     |             tick := signextend(2, tick)
  21 |     |             tickSpacing := signextend(2, tickSpacing)
  22 |     |             compressed :=
  23 |     |                 sub(
  24 |     |                     sdiv(tick, tickSpacing),
  25 |     |                     // if (tick < 0 && tick % tickSpacing != 0) then tick % tickSpacing < 0, vice versa
  26 |     |                     slt(smod(tick, tickSpacing), 0)
  27 |     |                 )
  28 |     |         }
  29 |     |     }
  30 |     | 
  31 |     |     /// @notice Computes the position in the mapping where the initialized bit for a tick lives
  32 |     |     /// @param tick The tick for which to compute the position
  33 |     |     /// @return wordPos The key in the mapping containing the word in which the bit is stored
  34 |     |     /// @return bitPos The bit position in the word where the flag is stored
  35 |     |     function position(int24 tick) internal pure returns (int16 wordPos, uint8 bitPos) {
  36 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
  37 |     |             // signed arithmetic shift right
  38 |     |             wordPos := sar(8, signextend(2, tick))
  39 |     |             bitPos := and(tick, 0xff)
  40 |     |         }
  41 |     |     }
  42 |     | 
  43 |     |     /// @notice Flips the initialized state for a given tick from false to true, or vice versa
  44 |     |     /// @param self The mapping in which to flip the tick
  45 |     |     /// @param tick The tick to flip
  46 |     |     /// @param tickSpacing The spacing between usable ticks
  47 | *   |     function flipTick(mapping(int16 => uint256) storage self, int24 tick, int24 tickSpacing) internal {
  48 |     |         // Equivalent to the following Solidity:
  49 |     |         //     if (tick % tickSpacing != 0) revert TickMisaligned(tick, tickSpacing);
  50 |     |         //     (int16 wordPos, uint8 bitPos) = position(tick / tickSpacing);
  51 |     |         //     uint256 mask = 1 << bitPos;
  52 |     |         //     self[wordPos] ^= mask;
  53 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
  54 |     |             tick := signextend(2, tick)
  55 |     |             tickSpacing := signextend(2, tickSpacing)
  56 |     |             // ensure that the tick is spaced
  57 |     |             if smod(tick, tickSpacing) {
  58 |     |                 let fmp := mload(0x40)
  59 |     |                 mstore(fmp, 0xd4d8f3e6) // selector for TickMisaligned(int24,int24)
  60 |     |                 mstore(add(fmp, 0x20), tick)
  61 |     |                 mstore(add(fmp, 0x40), tickSpacing)
  62 |     |                 revert(add(fmp, 0x1c), 0x44)
  63 |     |             }
  64 |     |             tick := sdiv(tick, tickSpacing)
  65 |     |             // calculate the storage slot corresponding to the tick
  66 |     |             // wordPos = tick >> 8
  67 |     |             mstore(0, sar(8, tick))
  68 |     |             mstore(0x20, self.slot)
  69 |     |             // the slot of self[wordPos] is keccak256(abi.encode(wordPos, self.slot))
  70 |     |             let slot := keccak256(0, 0x40)
  71 |     |             // mask = 1 << bitPos = 1 << (tick % 256)
  72 |     |             // self[wordPos] ^= mask
  73 |     |             sstore(slot, xor(sload(slot), shl(and(tick, 0xff), 1)))
  74 |     |         }
  75 |     |     }
  76 |     | 
  77 |     |     /// @notice Returns the next initialized tick contained in the same word (or adjacent word) as the tick that is either
  78 |     |     /// to the left (less than or equal to) or right (greater than) of the given tick
  79 |     |     /// @param self The mapping in which to compute the next initialized tick
  80 |     |     /// @param tick The starting tick
  81 |     |     /// @param tickSpacing The spacing between usable ticks
  82 |     |     /// @param lte Whether to search for the next initialized tick to the left (less than or equal to the starting tick)
  83 |     |     /// @return next The next initialized or uninitialized tick up to 256 ticks away from the current tick
  84 |     |     /// @return initialized Whether the next tick is initialized, as the function only searches within up to 256 ticks
  85 |     |     function nextInitializedTickWithinOneWord(
  86 |     |         mapping(int16 => uint256) storage self,
  87 |     |         int24 tick,
  88 |     |         int24 tickSpacing,
  89 |     |         bool lte
  90 |     |     ) internal view returns (int24 next, bool initialized) {
  91 |     |         unchecked {
  92 |     |             int24 compressed = compress(tick, tickSpacing);
  93 |     | 
  94 | *   |             if (lte) {
  95 |     |                 (int16 wordPos, uint8 bitPos) = position(compressed);
  96 |     |                 // all the 1s at or to the right of the current bitPos
  97 |     |                 uint256 mask = type(uint256).max >> (uint256(type(uint8).max) - bitPos);
  98 | *   |                 uint256 masked = self[wordPos] & mask;
  99 |     | 
 100 |     |                 // if there are no initialized ticks to the right of or at the current tick, return rightmost in the word
 101 | *   |                 initialized = masked != 0;
 102 |     |                 // overflow/underflow is possible, but prevented externally by limiting both tickSpacing and tick
 103 | *   |                 next = initialized
 104 | *   |                     ? (compressed - int24(uint24(bitPos - BitMath.mostSignificantBit(masked)))) * tickSpacing
 105 |     |                     : (compressed - int24(uint24(bitPos))) * tickSpacing;
 106 |     |             } else {
 107 |     |                 // start from the word of the next tick, since the current tick state doesn't matter
 108 |     |                 (int16 wordPos, uint8 bitPos) = position(++compressed);
 109 |     |                 // all the 1s at or to the left of the bitPos
 110 | *   |                 uint256 mask = ~((1 << bitPos) - 1);
 111 | *   |                 uint256 masked = self[wordPos] & mask;
 112 |     | 
 113 |     |                 // if there are no initialized ticks to the left of the current tick, return leftmost in the word
 114 | *   |                 initialized = masked != 0;
 115 |     |                 // overflow/underflow is possible, but prevented externally by limiting both tickSpacing and tick
 116 | *   |                 next = initialized
 117 |     |                     ? (compressed + int24(uint24(BitMath.leastSignificantBit(masked) - bitPos))) * tickSpacing
 118 |     |                     : (compressed + int24(uint24(type(uint8).max - bitPos))) * tickSpacing;
 119 |     |             }
 120 |     |         }
 121 |     |     }
 122 |     | }

  52 |     |     /// @notice Calculates sqrt(1.0001^tick) * 2^96

  54 |     |     /// @param tick The input tick for the above formula

  56 |     |     /// at the given tick
  57 | *   |     function getSqrtPriceAtTick(int24 tick) internal pure returns (uint160 sqrtPriceX96) {
  58 |     |         unchecked {
  59 |     |             uint256 absTick;
  60 | *   |             assembly ("memory-safe") {
  61 |     |                 tick := signextend(2, tick)
  62 |     |                 // mask = 0 if tick >= 0 else -1 (all 1s)
  63 |     |                 let mask := sar(255, tick)
  64 |     |                 // if tick >= 0, |tick| = tick = 0 ^ tick
  65 |     |                 // if tick < 0, |tick| = ~~|tick| = ~(-|tick| - 1) = ~(tick - 1) = (-1) ^ (tick - 1)
  66 |     |                 // either way, |tick| = mask ^ (tick + mask)
  67 |     |                 absTick := xor(mask, add(mask, tick))

  70 | *   |             if (absTick > uint256(int256(MAX_TICK))) InvalidTick.selector.revertWith(tick);

  73 |     |             // is calculated (using Q128.128). The constants used for this calculation are rounded to the nearest integer
  74 |     |

  28 |     | /// @title CurrencyLibrary
  29 |     | /// @dev This library allows for transferring and holding native tokens and ERC20 tokens
  30 |     | library CurrencyLibrary {
  31 |     |     /// @notice Additional context for ERC-7751 wrapped error when a native transfer fails
  32 |     |     error NativeTransferFailed();
  33 |     | 
  34 |     |     /// @notice Additional context for ERC-7751 wrapped error when an ERC20 transfer fails
  35 |     |     error ERC20TransferFailed();
  36 |     | 
  37 |     |     /// @notice A constant to represent the native currency
  38 |     |     Currency public constant ADDRESS_ZERO = Currency.wrap(address(0));
  39 |     | 
  40 | *   |     function transfer(Currency currency, address to, uint256 amount) internal {
  41 |     |         // altered from https://github.com/transmissions11/solmate/blob/44a9963d4c78111f77caa0e65d677b8b46d6f2e6/src/utils/SafeTransferLib.sol
  42 |     |         // modified custom error selectors
  43 |     | 
  44 |     |         bool success;
  45 | *   |         if (currency.isAddressZero()) {
  46 |     |             assembly ("memory-safe") {
  47 |     |                 // Transfer the ETH and revert if it fails.
  48 |     |                 success := call(gas(), to, amount, 0, 0, 0, 0)
  49 |     |             }
  50 |     |             // revert with NativeTransferFailed, containing the bubbled up error as an argument
  51 |     |             if (!success) {
  52 |     |                 CustomRevert.bubbleUpAndRevertWith(to, bytes4(0), NativeTransferFailed.selector);
  53 |     |             }
  54 |     |         } else {
  55 | *   |             assembly ("memory-safe") {
  56 |     |                 // Get a pointer to some free memory.
  57 |     |                 let fmp := mload(0x40)
  58 |     | 
  59 |     |                 // Write the abi-encoded calldata into memory, beginning with the function selector.
  60 |     |                 mstore(fmp, 0xa9059cbb00000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000)
  61 |     |                 mstore(add(fmp, 4), and(to, 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff)) // Append and mask the "to" argument.
  62 |     |                 mstore(add(fmp, 36), amount) // Append the "amount" argument. Masking not required as it's a full 32 byte type.
  63 |     | 
  64 |     |                 success :=
  65 |     |                     and(
  66 |     |                         // Set success to whether the call reverted, if not we check it either
  67 |     |                         // returned exactly 1 (can't just be non-zero data), or had no return data.
  68 |     |                         or(and(eq(mload(0), 1), gt(returndatasize(), 31)), iszero(returndatasize())),
  69 |     |                         // We use 68 because the length of our calldata totals up like so: 4 + 32 * 2.
  70 |     |                         // We use 0 and 32 to copy up to 32 bytes of return data into the scratch space.
  71 |     |                         // Counterintuitively, this call must be positioned second to the or() call in the
  72 |     |                         // surrounding and() call or else returndatasize() will be zero during the computation.
  73 |     |                         call(gas(), currency, 0, fmp, 68, 0, 32)
  74 |     |                     )
  75 |     | 
  76 |     |                 // Now clean the memory we used
  77 |     |                 mstore(fmp, 0) // 4 byte `selector` and 28 bytes of `to` were stored here
  78 |     |                 mstore(add(fmp, 0x20), 0) // 4 bytes of `to` and 28 bytes of `amount` were stored here
  79 |     |                 mstore(add(fmp, 0x40), 0) // 4 bytes of `amount` were stored here
  80 |     |             }
  81 |     |             // revert with ERC20TransferFailed, containing the bubbled up error as an argument
  82 | *   |             if (!success) {
  83 |     |                 CustomRevert.bubbleUpAndRevertWith(
  84 |     |                     Currency.unwrap(currency), IERC20Minimal.transfer.selector, ERC20TransferFailed.selector
  85 |     |                 );
  86 |     |             }
  87 |     |         }
  88 |     |     }

  92 |     |             return address(this).balance;

  2 |     | pragma solidity ^0.8.0;
  3 |     | 
  4 |     | /**
  5 |     |  * @dev Slot0 is a packed version of solidity structure.
  6 |     |  * Using the packaged version saves gas by not storing the structure fields in memory slots.
  7 |     |  *
  8 |     |  * Layout:
  9 |     |  * 24 bits empty | 24 bits lpFee | 12 bits protocolFee 1->0 | 12 bits protocolFee 0->1 | 24 bits tick | 160 bits sqrtPriceX96
 10 |     |  *
 11 |     |  * Fields in the direction from the least significant bit:
 12 |     |  *
 13 |     |  * The current price
 14 |     |  * uint160 sqrtPriceX96;
 15 |     |  *
 16 |     |  * The current tick
 17 |     |  * int24 tick;
 18 |     |  *
 19 |     |  * Protocol fee, expressed in hundredths of a bip, upper 12 bits are for 1->0, and the lower 12 are for 0->1
 20 |     |  * the maximum is 1000 - meaning the maximum protocol fee is 0.1%
 21 |     |  * the protocolFee is taken from the input first, then the lpFee is taken from the remaining input
 22 |     |  * uint24 protocolFee;
 23 |     |  *
 24 |     |  * The current LP fee of the pool. If the pool is dynamic, this does not include the dynamic fee flag.
 25 |     |  * uint24 lpFee;
 26 |     |  */
 27 |     | type Slot0 is bytes32;
 28 |     | 
 29 |     | using Slot0Library for Slot0 global;
 30 |     | 
 31 |     | /// @notice Library for getting and setting values in the Slot0 type
 32 |     | library Slot0Library {
 33 |     |     uint160 internal constant MASK_160_BITS = 0x00FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF;
 34 |     |     uint24 internal constant MASK_24_BITS = 0xFFFFFF;
 35 |     | 
 36 |     |     uint8 internal constant TICK_OFFSET = 160;
 37 |     |     uint8 internal constant PROTOCOL_FEE_OFFSET = 184;
 38 |     |     uint8 internal constant LP_FEE_OFFSET = 208;
 39 |     | 
 40 |     |     // #### GETTERS ####
 41 |     |     function sqrtPriceX96(Slot0 _packed) internal pure returns (uint160 _sqrtPriceX96) {
 42 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 43 |     |             _sqrtPriceX96 := and(MASK_160_BITS, _packed)
 44 |     |         }
 45 |     |     }
 46 |     | 
 47 |     |     function tick(Slot0 _packed) internal pure returns (int24 _tick) {
 48 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 49 |     |             _tick := signextend(2, shr(TICK_OFFSET, _packed))
 50 |     |         }
 51 |     |     }
 52 |     | 
 53 |     |     function protocolFee(Slot0 _packed) internal pure returns (uint24 _protocolFee) {
 54 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 55 |     |             _protocolFee := and(MASK_24_BITS, shr(PROTOCOL_FEE_OFFSET, _packed))
 56 |     |         }
 57 |     |     }
 58 |     | 
 59 |     |     function lpFee(Slot0 _packed) internal pure returns (uint24 _lpFee) {
 60 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 61 |     |             _lpFee := and(MASK_24_BITS, shr(LP_FEE_OFFSET, _packed))
 62 |     |         }
 63 |     |     }
 64 |     | 
 65 |     |     // #### SETTERS ####
 66 |     |     function setSqrtPriceX96(Slot0 _packed, uint160 _sqrtPriceX96) internal pure returns (Slot0 _result) {
 67 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 68 |     |             _result := or(and(not(MASK_160_BITS), _packed), and(MASK_160_BITS, _sqrtPriceX96))
 69 |     |         }
 70 |     |     }
 71 |     | 
 72 |     |     function setTick(Slot0 _packed, int24 _tick) internal pure returns (Slot0 _result) {
 73 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 74 |     |             _result := or(and(not(shl(TICK_OFFSET, MASK_24_BITS)), _packed), shl(TICK_OFFSET, and(MASK_24_BITS, _tick)))
 75 |     |         }
 76 |     |     }
 77 |     | 
 78 |     |     function setProtocolFee(Slot0 _packed, uint24 _protocolFee) internal pure returns (Slot0 _result) {
 79 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 80 |     |             _result :=
 81 |     |                 or(
 82 |     |                     and(not(shl(PROTOCOL_FEE_OFFSET, MASK_24_BITS)), _packed),
 83 |     |                     shl(PROTOCOL_FEE_OFFSET, and(MASK_24_BITS, _protocolFee))
 84 |     |                 )
 85 |     |         }
 86 |     |     }
 87 |     | 
 88 |     |     function setLpFee(Slot0 _packed, uint24 _lpFee) internal pure returns (Slot0 _result) {
 89 | *   |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 90 |     |             _result :=
 91 |     |                 or(and(not(shl(LP_FEE_OFFSET, MASK_24_BITS)), _packed), shl(LP_FEE_OFFSET, and(MASK_24_BITS, _lpFee)))
 92 |     |         }

 288 |     |     /// @dev Calling increase with 0 liquidity will credit the caller with any underlying fees of the position
 289 |     |     function _increase(
 290 |     |         uint256 tokenId,
 291 |     |         uint256 liquidity,
 292 |     |         uint128 amount0Max,
 293 |     |         uint128 amount1Max,
 294 |     |         bytes calldata hookData
 295 |     |     ) internal virtual onlyIfApproved(msgSender(), tokenId) {
 296 |     |         (PoolKey memory poolKey, PositionInfo info) = getPoolAndPositionInfo(tokenId);
 297 |     | 
 298 |     |         // Note: The tokenId is used as the salt for this position, so every minted position has unique storage in the pool manager.
 299 |     |         (BalanceDelta liquidityDelta, BalanceDelta feesAccrued) =
 300 |     |             _modifyLiquidity(info, poolKey, liquidity.toInt256(), bytes32(tokenId), hookData);
 301 |     |         // Slippage checks should be done on the principal liquidityDelta which is the liquidityDelta - feesAccrued
 302 |     |         (liquidityDelta - feesAccrued).validateMaxIn(amount0Max, amount1Max);
 303 |     |     }

 305 |     |     /// @notice DEPRECATED: Vulnerable to sandwich attacks - do not use this function.

  1 |     | // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
  2 |     | pragma solidity ^0.8.0;
  3 |     | 
  4 |     | import {IEIP712_v4} from "../interfaces/IEIP712_v4.sol";
  5 |     | 
  6 |     | /// @notice Generic EIP712 implementation
  7 |     | /// @dev Maintains cross-chain replay protection in the event of a fork
  8 |     | /// @dev Should not be delegatecall'd because DOMAIN_SEPARATOR returns the cached hash and does not recompute with the delegatecallers address
  9 |     | /// @dev Reference: https://github.com/Uniswap/permit2/blob/3f17e8db813189a03950dc7fc8382524a095c053/src/EIP712.sol
 10 |     | /// @dev Reference: https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/blob/7bd2b2aaf68c21277097166a9a51eb72ae239b34/contracts/utils/cryptography/EIP712.sol
 11 |     | contract EIP712_v4 is IEIP712_v4 {
 12 |     |     // Cache the domain separator as an immutable value, but also store the chain id that it
 13 |     |     // corresponds to, in order to invalidate the cached domain separator if the chain id changes.
 14 |     |     bytes32 private immutable _CACHED_DOMAIN_SEPARATOR;
 15 |     |     uint256 private immutable _CACHED_CHAIN_ID;
 16 |     |     bytes32 private immutable _HASHED_NAME;
 17 |     | 
 18 |     |     bytes32 private constant _TYPE_HASH =
 19 | *   |         keccak256("EIP712Domain(string name,uint256 chainId,address verifyingContract)");
 20 |     | 
 21 |     |     constructor(string memory name) {
 22 | *   |         _HASHED_NAME = keccak256(bytes(name));
 23 |     | 
 24 | *   |         _CACHED_CHAIN_ID = block.chainid;
 25 | *   |         _CACHED_DOMAIN_SEPARATOR = _buildDomainSeparator();
 26 |     |     }
 27 |     | 
 28 |     |     /// @inheritdoc IEIP712_v4
 29 | *   |     function DOMAIN_SEPARATOR() public view returns (bytes32) {
 30 |     |         // uses cached version if chainid is unchanged from construction
 31 |     |         return block.chainid == _CACHED_CHAIN_ID ? _CACHED_DOMAIN_SEPARATOR : _buildDomainSeparator();
 32 |     |     }
 33 |     | 
 34 |     |     /// @notice Builds a domain separator using the current chainId and contract address.
 35 |     |     function _buildDomainSeparator() private view returns (bytes32) {
 36 | *   |         return keccak256(abi.encode(_TYPE_HASH, _HASHED_NAME, block.chainid, address(this)));
 37 |     |     }
 38 |     | 
 39 |     |     /// @notice Creates an EIP-712 typed data hash
 40 |     |     function _hashTypedData(bytes32 dataHash) internal view returns (bytes32 digest) {
 41 |     |         // equal to keccak256(abi.encodePacked("\x19\x01", DOMAIN_SEPARATOR(), dataHash));
 42 |     |         bytes32 domainSeparator = DOMAIN_SEPARATOR();
 43 |     |         assembly ("memory-safe") {
 44 |     |             let fmp := mload(0x40)
 45 |     |             mstore(fmp, hex"1901")
 46 |     |             mstore(add(fmp, 0x02), domainSeparator)
 47 |     |             mstore(add(fmp, 0x22), dataHash)
 48 |     |             digest := keccak256(fmp, 0x42)
 49 |     | 
 50 |     |             // now clean the memory we used
 51 |     |             mstore(fmp, 0) // fmp held "\x19\x01", domainSeparator
 52 |     |             mstore(add(fmp, 0x20), 0) // fmp+0x20 held domainSeparator, dataHash
 53 |     |             mstore(add(fmp, 0x40), 0) // fmp+0x40 held dataHash
 54 |     |         }
 55 |     |     }
 56 |     | }

  52 |     |         signature.verify(_hashTypedData(digest), owner);
  53 |     |

 10 |     |     function multicall(bytes[] calldata data) external payable returns (bytes[] memory results) {
 11 |     |         results = new bytes[](data.length);
 12 |     |         for (uint256 i = 0; i < data.length; i++) {
 13 |     |             (bool success, bytes memory result) = address(this).delegatecall(data[i]);
 14 |     |

 16 |     |                 // bubble up the revert reason
 17 |     |                 assembly {
 18 |     |                     revert(add(result, 0x20), mload(result))
 19 |     |                 }
 20 |     |             }
 21 |     | 
 22 |     |             results[i] = result;
 23 |     |         }

  8 |     | contract UnorderedNonce is IUnorderedNonce {
  9 |     |     /// @inheritdoc IUnorderedNonce
 10 |     |     mapping(address owner => mapping(uint256 word => uint256 bitmap)) public nonces;
 11 |     | 
 12 |     |     /// @notice Consume a nonce, reverting if it has already been used
 13 |     |     /// @param owner address, the owner/signer of the nonce
 14 |     |     /// @param nonce uint256, the nonce to consume. The top 248 bits are the word, the bottom 8 bits indicate the bit position
 15 |     |     function _useUnorderedNonce(address owner, uint256 nonce) internal {
 16 |     |         uint256 wordPos = nonce >> 8;
 17 |     |         uint256 bitPos = uint8(nonce);
 18 |     | 
 19 |     |         uint256 bit = 1 << bitPos;
 20 |     |         uint256 flipped = nonces[owner][wordPos] ^= bit;
 21 |     |         if (flipped & bit == 0) revert NonceAlreadyUsed();
 22 |     |     }
 23 |     | 
 24 |     |     /// @inheritdoc IUnorderedNonce
 25 |     |     function revokeNonce(uint256 nonce) external payable {
 26 |     |         _useUnorderedNonce(msg.sender, nonce);
 27 |     |     }

  9 |     | interface ISubscriber {

 14 |     |

 17 |     |     /// @dev Because of EIP-150, solidity may only allocate 63/64 of gasleft()

 28 |     |         external;
 29 |     | 
 30 |     |     /// @notice Called when a position modifies its liquidity or collects fees
 31 |     |     /// @param tokenId the token ID of the position
 32 |     |     /// @param liquidityChange the change in liquidity on the underlying position
